arguments.body:
# Q1 2027 platform workstreams — Lantern, Guardrails, and owner map

Owner of this document: Alex (reviewer role: shared-contract and failure-boundary).
Status as of 2027-02-05: living document. Sections below reflect the December 17
final decision, the December 28 kickoff-prep framing, the December 29 participant
proposals, the January 11 staff-only rehearsal acceptance checklist, the January 22
Q1 joint handoff rehearsal result (M–P), the February 4 source-side correction
(Cyrus republish of 2 Cardinality Guardrails records), the February 4 wording close
(Iris on the corrected staff-only reference slice), and the February 5–18 internal
operating observation (Q–S). Nothing here authorizes customer exposure or transfers
routine implementation ownership to Alex.

================================================================
1. APPROVED SPLIT (unchanged from December 17 review)
================================================================

Q1 2027 is three linked workstreams, not one Lantern monolith:

  - Lantern          — owns explanation and navigation. Reference-only.
  - Cardinality      — owns pipeline limits and cost semantics (authoritative).
    Guardrails
  - Owner map        — owns published responsibility (authoritative).

Lantern implementation is owned by Product Engineering. Alex is not the routine
implementation gate for any of the three workstreams. Alex reviews the shared
five-field contract and the cross-system failure boundaries only.

Lantern does not absorb owner-map data or Cardinality Guardrails data. Lantern
does not write into published responsibility. Lantern does not place limit or
cost data on a customer surface.

================================================================
2. FIVE-FIELD SHARED REFERENCE CONTRACT
================================================================

Per the December 17 review, internal Lantern cards may navigate staff to
authoritative owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails records using ONLY these
five fields — no others:

  1. tenant_id
  2. canonical_service_id
  3. authority_type
  4. authority_record_id
  5. source_timestamp

Rules of use:
  - Each reference carries exactly these five fields and nothing more.
  - Owner-map references and Cardinality Guardrails references carry
    SEPARATE authority identities and SEPARATE source timestamps — they
    are not collapsed into one reference and never share an
    authority_record_id.
  - If an authority record is stale (source_timestamp older than the
    freshness threshold for that authority_type) or missing (no current
    authority_record_id), Lantern MUST render the reference as explicit
    "unknown" with the stale/missing field shown — it does NOT guess,
    default, copy from cache, or fall back to a payload value.
  - Lantern MUST NOT copy any authority payload value into the card.
  - Lantern MUST NOT offer mutation capability into either authority.
  - On a denial (stale, missing, or out-of-scope), Lantern MUST NOT issue
    any adapter call afterwards. Zero adapter calls after denial.
  - These rules apply equally to staff-only and internal-shadow surfaces.

================================================================
3. JANUARY 22 STAFF-ONLY REHEARSAL — ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST
================================================================

Rehearsal date: 2027-01-22. Audience: staff only. Purpose: dry-run the
internal operating use of Lantern references against live authority records,
under the December 17 rules. The rehearsal is NOT a customer-exposure
authorization and is NOT a transfer of routine implementation ownership to
Alex. Product Engineering remains the implementation owner for the rehearsal
slice. Alex reviews whether the slice meets this checklist.

Pass criteria — every item MUST hold. A single failure blocks "passed."

  [A] Reference shape
      A.1  Every Lantern reference emitted during the rehearsal carries
           ONLY tenant_id, canonical_service_id, authority_type,
           authority_record_id, and source_timestamp.
      A.2  No reference carries any additional field, annotation, payload
           value, computed derivation, or display string derived from the
           authority payload.

  [B] Separate identities and source timestamps
      B.1  Every owner-map reference carries its own authority_record_id
           and its own source_timestamp.
      B.2  Every Cardinality Guardrails reference carries its own
           authority_record_id and its own source_timestamp.
      B.3  No reference shares an authority_record_id between owner-map
           and Cardinality Guardrails.
      B.4  No reference collapses the two authorities into a single
           combined reference.

  [C] Stale or missing authority records
      C.1  A reference whose source_timestamp is older than the freshness
           threshold for its authority_type is rendered as EXPLICIT
           "unknown — stale authority_record" with the
           authority_record_id and source_timestamp still shown (no
           hiding, no caching past the value).
      C.2  A reference with no current authority_record_id is rendered as
           EXPLICIT "unknown — no current authority_record" with
           tenant_id and canonical_service_id still shown.
      C.3  No reference defaults, fabricates, or back-fills a missing or
           stale authority_record_id.

  [D] Zero adapter calls after denial
      D.1  After a denial (stale, missing, out-of-scope, or unsupported
           authority_type), the rehearsal slice makes ZERO adapter calls
           to the owner-map system or to Cardinality Guardrails for the
           same (tenant_id, canonical_service_id) pair.
      D.2  Adapter-call counts before vs. after denial are recorded in
           the rehearsal evidence; the post-denial count is exactly zero.

  [E] No payload copy, no mutation path
      E.1  No Lantern card in the rehearsal displays a copied authority
           payload value (no copied limit value, no copied cost value,
           no copied published-responsibility text).
      E.2  No Lantern card in the rehearsal exposes or links to a
           mutation path into the owner map or into Cardinality
           Guardrails.

  [F] No Harbor Health or Mosaic Commerce surface
      F.1  No authority payload value, mutation path, or customer-path
           request, artifact, or output for Harbor Health is produced,
           referenced, copied, or implied by the rehearsal.
      F.2  No authority payload value, mutation path, or customer-path
           request, artifact, or output for Mosaic Commerce is produced,
           referenced, copied, or implied by the rehearsal.
      F.3  Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce remain absent from the
           rehearsal surface exactly as they were absent on December 17.

  [G] Boundary preservation
      G.1  Lantern remains the explanation and navigation layer; it does
           not become authoritative for pipeline limits, cost semantics,
           or published responsibility.
      G.2  Cardinality Guardrails remains authoritative for pipeline
           limits and cost semantics.
      G.3  The owner map remains authoritative for published
           responsibility.
      G.4  Product Engineering remains the implementation owner of the
           Lantern rehearsal slice; Alex does not become the routine
           implementation gate.

  [H] Out-of-scope statement (recorded at the top of the rehearsal
      evidence)
      H.1  The rehearsal evidence states plainly that passing the
           rehearsal would neither authorize customer exposure for any
           tenant nor make Alex the routine implementation gate for
           Lantern, Cardinality Guardrails, or the owner map.
      H.2  The same statement is reproduced in the post-rehearsal
           summary.

Recording rule: each item above is checked once with PASS / FAIL / NOT
OBSERVED, with the timestamp of the check and the name of the staff
member who verified it. FAIL on any single item blocks "passed." Items
not observed during the rehearsal (e.g. mutation path) are marked NOT
OBSERVED with a one-line reason, not left blank.

================================================================
4. KICKOFF-PREP (carried from December 28; reframed by January 11)
================================================================

The January 7 kickoff is a decision session, not a broad status review.
The January 22 rehearsal is the next operating-use checkpoint after that
session; this document is now the rehearsal-prep document as well as the
workstreams brief.

Interfaces that need agreement at or before January 7:
  - The five-field reference contract (section 2) is the only contract
    shape that crosses the three workstreams.
  - Freshness thresholds for each authority_type must be named by the
    owner of that authority. A missing threshold is treated as
    "unknown" until named.
  - Denial semantics — what counts as stale, missing, or out-of-scope —
    must be agreed before the rehearsal so the zero-adapter-after-denial
    check has a deterministic trigger.

First-deliverable decisions expected on January 7:
  - Confirm or revise the three-workstream split (default: confirm).
  - Name freshness thresholds for owner-map authority_type and for
    Cardinality Guardrails authority_type.
  - Confirm Product Engineering as implementation owner for the Lantern
    rehearsal slice, with Alex reviewing only against the checklist in
    section 3.

Customer authorization and routine implementation ownership are out of
scope for both the kickoff and the rehearsal.

================================================================
5. PARTICIPANT PROPOSALS (pending January 7 decisions)
================================================================

Recorded 2026-12-29. None of these are approved deliverables or ownership
changes. Outcomes will be recorded after the January 7 decision session,
not before.

  Iris — Lantern reference navigation: internal interpretation and
          wording check over Lantern's reference navigation, against the
          five-field contract.

  Cyrus — Cardinality Guardrails: versioned authority-record interface
          that keeps pipeline limits and cost semantics authoritative
          in Cardinality Guardrails.

  Wes   — metrics-router operating controls: inventory mapping each
          control to its authoritative record and current operating
          evidence.

  Product Engineering — first Lantern implementation slice consuming
          the references without copying authority values and without
          adding mutation.

  Alex  — review of the five-field shared contract and cross-system
          failure boundaries only. Not the implementation gate.

================================================================
6. OPEN QUESTIONS (carry forward)
================================================================

  - Freshness thresholds per authority_type — pending owner naming.
  - Whether the January 22 rehearsal will exercise a deny path (stale or
    missing) on purpose to verify section 3[D]. Pending Iris / Cyrus
    confirmation.
  - Whether the rehearsal evidence will be appended to the existing
    internal-shadow evidence document or kept in this document.
    Pending Hema's call.

================================================================
7. REFERENCES
================================================================

  - doc_lantern_v0_arch — Lantern v0 architecture (existing).
  - doc_abc1ea0ce51646b09a28f09a988fbaf6 — Lantern platform-reference
    rehearsal (existing).
  - doc_da078d82f4014789836b26d9a0271c8c — Lantern dual-authority
    internal shadow (existing).
  - doc_2997752452ce42029b0a0f3d993755f8 — Lantern shared-integration
    continuation decision record (existing).
  - December 17 review decision (recorded in #lantern and in this doc).
  - November 17 internal-shadow observation (appended to the internal-
    shadow evidence document).

================================================================
Q1 JOINT HANDOFF REHEARSAL #1 — 2027-01-22 — RESULT (NOT APPROVAL)
================================================================

This addendum records the actual outcome of the first Q1 staff-only joint
handoff rehearsal on 2027-01-22. It is a result, not an approval. It does
NOT authorize customer exposure, does NOT release the corrected
implementation, does NOT re-open the five-field contract, and does NOT
change the ownership split or Alex's bounded review role. Prior content
(approved split, five-field contract, January 22 staff-only rehearsal
acceptance checklist, kickoff-prep, participant proposals, open
questions, references) remains in force.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
M. INVENTORY AND NAVIGATION RESULT
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  M.1  Wes (owner of metrics-router control mapping) inventoried
       11 current metrics-router control mappings for the rehearsal.

  M.2  Product Engineering (implementation owner of the rehearsal slice)
       demonstrated correct navigation for 9 of the 11 references.
       Navigation surfaced the authoritative record in Cardinality
       Guardrails or the owner map without copying values, per the
       reference-only contract and the §J.6 single-authority assertion.

  M.3  Navigation was UNAVAILABLE for the remaining 2 records. Reason
       is recorded in §N, not here; this section records only the
       11-inventory / 9-nav-OK / 2-blocked count.

  M.4  The 9-of-11 navigation result is a POSITIVE OBSERVATION against
       the rehearsal acceptance checklist group A (reference shape) and
       group B (separate identities and source timestamps) for the
       9 records that navigated cleanly. It is NOT an approval of the
       corrected implementation overall; the 2 blocked records (N)
       are part of the same rehearsal and gate the result.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
N. TWO CARDINALITY GUARDRAILS RECORDS — SOURCE-IDENTITY BLOCK
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  N.1  The 2 blocked records are Cardinality Guardrails records that
       identify metrics-router only by display name. They OMIT the
       required `canonical_service_id` (the platform-reference canonical
       id per §2). Without `canonical_service_id`, alias resolution
       per §2 cannot resolve, and the reference cannot navigate to
       the authoritative record.

  N.2  What Lantern did NOT do (this is the contract-bound behavior,
       not a missing feature):
         N.2.1  Lantern did NOT infer a UI alias from the display name.
         N.2.2  Lantern did NOT copy a fallback identity onto the
                reference.
         N.2.3  Lantern did NOT mutate the owner map to attach a
                canonical id.
         N.2.4  Lantern did NOT bypass the reference-only contract
                to present a copy of the record's values as its own.
       Each of those would have violated either §J.3 (what the contract
       may not contain), §J.6 (single-authority assertion), or §I.2.3
       (no owner-map write path from Lantern). The block is the
       contract working as designed.

  N.3  The block is recorded against the rehearsal acceptance
       checklist:
         - Group A (reference shape): the missing `canonical_service_id`
           is a contract-shape failure on the source record, not on
           the Lantern reference. PASS for the 9 navigated references;
           FAIL (source-side) for the 2 blocked records.
         - Group B (separate identities): cannot be evaluated for
           the 2 blocked records because identity is absent.
           NOT OBSERVED for those 2, by reason "no
           canonical_service_id on source".
         - Group F (no Harbor Health / Mosaic Commerce surface):
           unaffected; the 2 blocked records are metrics-router
           control-mapping records and did not surface to either
           customer path. PASS.
         - All other checklist groups: unaffected by the block;
           recorded against the 9 navigated references per M.4.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
O. CORRECTION OWNERSHIP — CYRUS (CARDINALITY GUARDRAILS)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  O.1  Cyrus owns Cardinality Guardrails and is the authoritative
       source for the 2 blocked records. The correction is on the
       source side, not on the Lantern side.

  O.2  Required correction (binding on Cyrus, not on Alex):
         O.2.1  Republish the 2 Cardinality Guardrails records with
                the canonical metrics-router identity, specifically
                populating `canonical_service_id` from the canonical
                id set, not from the display name.
         O.2.2  PRESERVE the original authoritative source_timestamp
                on each record. The republish is a source-side
                correction of identity, not a re-issue that resets
                the record's authoritative timestamp. This keeps
                the §F (F.1, F.3) source-timestamp rule intact and
                prevents a regression on group C (stale-or-missing
                authority).
         O.2.3  Do NOT alter any other field on the record except
                what's required to carry the canonical identity.
                Operating limits, cost semantics, and freshness
                markers stay in Cardinality Guardrails per §I.2.1,
                §I.2.2, §J.6; they are not in scope for this
                correction.

  O.3  Alex's role on the correction: NONE on the republish itself.
       Alex remains on shared-contract / failure-boundary review.
       Specifically, Alex does NOT author the canonical id, does NOT
       override Cyrus on the republish shape, and does NOT shortcut
       the §F source-timestamp rule.

  O.4  Iris's role on the correction: confirms, once republished,
       that the navigation / explanation role (J.5) holds for the
       corrected records. Pending; not granted here.

  O.5  Wes's role on the correction: confirms the canonical
       metrics-router id used by Cyrus is the one Wes inventoried.
       Pending; not granted here.

  O.6  Product Engineering's role on the correction: reruns the
       rehearsal slice against the 2 corrected records and produces
       executable evidence that navigation now succeeds for those
       references under the unchanged five-field contract. Pending;
       not run here.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
P. HANDOFF STATUS — STILL BLOCKED, PENDING CORRECTED RERUN
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  P.1  The shared Q1 handoff REMAINS BLOCKED. The 2027-01-22 rehearsal
       did NOT clear the gate; it produced a partial result
       (9-of-11 navigation) plus a precise source-side failure
       (2 blocked records, identity missing), and that failure is
       the gate.

  P.2  Unblocking requires ALL of the following, in order:
         P.2.1  Cyrus republishes the 2 Cardinality Guardrails
                records per §O.2, preserving source_timestamp.
         P.2.2  Wes confirms the canonical id matches the
                inventory (O.5).
         P.2.3  Iris confirms the navigation / explanation role
                still holds under J.5 for the corrected records
                (O.4).
         P.2.4  Product Engineering reruns the rehearsal slice and
                produces executable evidence that navigation succeeds
                for all 11 references under the unchanged five-field
                contract (O.6).
         P.2.5  Alex reviews the executable evidence against the
                January 22 staff-only rehearsal acceptance checklist
                (groups A–H) and records PASS / FAIL / NOT OBSERVED
                per the checklist's recording rule.

  P.3  The rerun is a COMPLETE rerun, not a partial rerun over the
       2 corrected records only. Reason: the 9 previously-navigated
       references must be re-confirmed under the same evidence bar
       as the 2 corrected ones, so that no record carries an
       evidence gap created by the republish.

  P.4  Until P.2.1–P.2.5 all complete:
         - The five-field contract is unchanged (§J).
         - The ownership split is unchanged (M.4 carries forward).
         - Alex's review role is unchanged (shared-contract /
           failure-boundary only).
         - No customer scope expansion for Harbor Health or
           Mosaic Commerce (§K).
         - No authorization expansion for either account (§K.2).
         - No post-3/31 authorization implied or granted.

================================================================
SOURCE-SIDE CORRECTION AND WORDING CLOSE — 2027-02-04
================================================================

This addendum records two 2027-02-04 events that advance §P.2.1 and §P.2.3
WITHOUT releasing the handoff. It does NOT authorize customer exposure,
does NOT release the corrected implementation, does NOT re-open the
five-field contract, does NOT change the ownership split, and does NOT
change Alex's bounded review role. §M–§P remain in force; the handoff
remains blocked pending the corrected rerun evidence (§P.2.4) and Alex's
checklist review (§P.2.5).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q. CYRUS REPUBLISH — 2027-02-04 (§P.2.1 satisfied)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Q.1  On 2027-02-04 Cyrus republished the 2 Cardinality Guardrails
       records identified in §N. The republish used the
       guardrails.authority.v1 interface and was an IDENTITY-ONLY
       correction: `canonical_service_id` was populated to point at
       metrics-router, and the original authoritative source_timestamp
       on each record was PRESERVED (no reset).

  Q.2  The republish did NOT carry payload, did NOT mutate other
       fields, and was internal-only. Operating limits, cost
       semantics, and freshness markers on the 2 records remain in
       Cardinality Guardrails per §I.2.1, §I.2.2, §J.6; this
       correction is bounded to identity.

  Q.3  Effect on §P.2: P.2.1 is now SATISFIED. P.2.2 (Wes canonical-id
       confirmation), P.2.3 (Iris wording confirmation against the
       corrected slice), P.2.4 (Product Engineering rerun evidence),
       and P.2.5 (Alex checklist review) remain pending.

  Q.4  Effect on §N: the source-side block on the 2 records is now
       RESOLVED at the source. Navigation will be re-evaluated against
       the corrected records during the rerun (§P.2.4), not here.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
R. IRIS WORDING CLOSE — 2027-02-04 (§P.2.3 satisfied)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  R.1  On 2027-02-04 Iris closed the wording check on the corrected
       staff-only reference slice (the wording review that had been
       pending since the 2027-01-19 sentence review). The close was
       on the corrected slice, i.e. the slice that will be exercised
       against the §Q.1 corrected Cardinality Guardrails records.

  R.2  Wording standard Iris confirmed: every card on the corrected
       staff-only reference slice names owner-map and Cardinality
       Guardrails as the AUTHORITIES; Lantern is named as the
       explanation and navigation layer only. No card claims that
       Lantern OWNS a value, OWNS control, or WRITES control. No
       card asserts that Lantern is authoritative for pipeline
       limits, cost semantics, or published responsibility.

  R.3  Effect on §P.2: P.2.3 is now SATISFIED at the wording layer.
       The wording close is a precondition for the operating-use
       exercise; it does NOT, by itself, exercise navigation. P.2.2,
       P.2.4, and P.2.5 remain pending.

  R.4  Effect on §M.4 / §G.1 / §J.6: the wording close reinforces
       (does not replace) those assertions. The single-authority
       assertion (J.6) is preserved; Lantern remains
       explanation-and-navigation only; Product Engineering remains
       the implementation owner of the slice. Alex's review role is
       unchanged.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
S. INTERNAL OPERATING OBSERVATION — 2027-02-05 THROUGH 2027-02-18
   (EVIDENCE COLLECTION; NOT COMPLETION; NOT AUTHORIZATION)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  S.1  SCOPE OF THIS SECTION. This section opens the two-week
       internal operating observation on the corrected first Q1
       reference slice. The observation runs 2027-02-05 through
       2027-02-18. It is the operating-use vehicle for §P.2.4
       (Product Engineering rerun evidence) and §P.2.5 (Alex
       checklist review); §Q cleared P.2.1 and §R cleared P.2.3, so
       this window is where the rerun is exercised and Alex's review
       is recorded. Wes's owner-led operating review (§S.4) is the
       operational form of the §P.2.2 confirmation.

  S.2  WHAT THIS OBSERVATION IS.
         S.2.1  Staff-only operating use of the corrected Lantern
                reference slice against the live, §Q-corrected
                Cardinality Guardrails records and against the live
                owner map.
         S.2.2  Evidence collection under the January 22 staff-only
                rehearsal acceptance checklist (groups A–H), now
                exercised in operating use rather than rehearsal.
         S.2.3  An owner-led operating review of all 11 metrics-router
                controls (Wes), an authority-wording sweep on the
                staff-only slice (Iris), and a separate customer-path
                audit of Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce for any
                request, artifact, or output from the internal
                integration (Product Engineering).

  S.3  WHAT THIS OBSERVATION IS NOT.
         S.3.1  NOT a release of the handoff. The handoff is released
                only after §P.2.4 evidence is in hand and §P.2.5

arguments.body:
**v0 addendum — ownership cards: provenance-or-omit rule (2023-07-31)**

Capturing a rule change forced by the first real owner-map import into Lantern's derived read model, before it gets lost. This sits alongside the 7/13 addendum, the 7/18 contract comment, and the 7/20 contract lock.

**The gap the import exposed.** The rollup-service and alerting/dashboards ownership-change cards have enough surrounding context that a human reviewer can guess the current owner from the surrounding records. The imported records themselves do not carry enough recorded provenance for the UI to *prove* why the ownership state is true. Iris flagged the UX problem immediately: if the surface shows guessed cards, Lantern looks authoritative while the missing evidence is hidden. That is the exact failure mode the provenance boundary is supposed to prevent, not just defer.

**The rule, locked for v0.**

- An ownership card only appears in the surface when the underlying event carries recorded provenance sufficient to prove the ownership state. Provenance is the recorded `source_ref` + `actor` + `source_system` + `collected_at` + `transform_version` object — not context, not surrounding cards, not a human's plausible inference.
- If an imported ownership record does not carry the provenance required to prove its ownership state, it stays out of the surface. It is not surfaced with a caveat, not rendered as a "best guess" chip, not shown in a weaker style. It is omitted.
- The UI must not infer ownership state from contextual clues, even when a human reviewer would land on the right owner. "A human could guess it" is not a substitute for recorded provenance. The derived read model is a join over recorded facts; inferred joins are the anti-pattern this whole direction was set up to avoid.
- Apparent gaps in the surface are a signal, not a bug. When the surface looks sparse because ownership records are missing provenance, that is the system working as designed — it tells us the ownership emitter for that service needs to be wired to record provenance, not that the surface should paper over the gap.

**Why this rule and not a softer version.** A "show with a weaker style" path still presents inferred ownership as a fact in the UI, which is the same provenance gap wearing a different hat. A "show with a caveat" path puts the burden of evaluating evidence on every PM who sees the card, which is exactly the audience that should not be evaluating evidence — they should be reading outcomes. The clean line is: provenance recorded → surface it; provenance not recorded → omit it. No third state.

**Scope.** This is a v0 rule on ownership cards specifically. The general "UI reads from derived read model, no inferred hidden transitions" rule from the 7/20 contract lock still stands; this addendum is the operationalization of that rule for the ownership card, written down because the import made the gap concrete.

Filed as an addendum rather than a doc rewrite so the rule is visible in the review thread where Iris/Hema/Theo will see it before any v0.1 ownership-card work lands. Happy to fold it into the doc body once reviewers ack.

messages.content:
LANTERN query_volume_delta — field review against locked architecture

Iris asks for data_quality + an experimental flag in the envelope so UI can dogfood-style without implying source-of-truth. Theo is fine if v0 stays internal-dogfood-only as long as the demo shows signal. Your field list mapped against the locked conventions (surface enum, data_quality sub-enums, append-only facts, rename-is-breaking rule).

Tensions to resolve first

  1. Iris's "complete|estimated|partial" does not match the locked data_quality.completeness enum, which is complete|partial|unknown. Two paths:
     a. Reconcile in conversation — tell Iris "estimated" maps to partial (data present, coverage incomplete) or unknown (haven't yet determined). Stick with the locked enum.
     b. Add "estimated" to the enum. That is a breaking change to data_quality and ripples to every other Lantern fact that uses it — only worth it if Iris's UI hook genuinely needs the distinction.
     Default to (a). The locked enum already covers what "estimated" implies, and experimental + data_quality.notes give Iris room to express nuance without touching the enum.

  2. `delta_percent` is a rename of the established `delta` field. Per your architecture rule, renaming is breaking and requires a schema-version bump. Either keep `delta` (with units documented in the field itself or in data_quality.notes) or formally bump and call it `delta_percent`.

  3. `visibility` vs `experimental` — not redundant if scoped correctly:
       visibility   = the surface/channel this fact routes to (internal_dogfood for v0; pm_v0 once Iris signs off)
       experimental = per-instance UI hint for dogfood styling (this is what Iris actually asked for)
     For this event in v0, visibility is constant (internal_dogfood) but experimental can vary per event.

Field-by-field map

  event_id          append-only fact ID, UUID or ULID
  event_type        constant "query_volume_delta"
  observed_at       wall-clock when the fact was recorded
  service           what was measured (e.g. rollup-service)
  source_system     origin tier of the metrics pipeline
  emitting_adapter  which Lantern adapter wrote it
  provenance_url    link back to source / lineage; nullable
  window_start/end  measurement window (ISO ts)
  baseline_window   comparison window — object {start,end} or duration+offset; pick one and document
  delta_percent     see tension #2
  data_quality      {completeness, confidence, notes} per locked enums; notes capped, absent when unused
  visibility        "internal_dogfood" | "pm_v0" — channel/surface marker
  experimental      boolean per-instance UI flag

Proposed envelope shape

  {
    "event_id": "...",
    "event_type": "query_volume_delta",
    "observed_at": "2023-07-11T...",
    "service": "rollup-service",
    "source_system": "metrics-rollup",
    "emitting_adapter": "lantern.rollup-adapter",
    "provenance_url": "https://...",
    "window_start": "2023-07-11T11:05:00Z",
    "window_end":   "2023-07-11T11:10:00Z",
    "baseline_window": {
      "start": "2023-07-11T11:00:00Z",
      "end":   "2023-07-11T11:05:00Z"
    },
    "delta_percent": -18.0,
    "data_quality": {
      "completeness": "complete",
      "confidence":   "medium",
      "notes":        "rollup lag at 92%, partial coverage"
    },
    "visibility":   "internal_dogfood",
    "experimental": true
  }

What I want from you before this is final

  - Reconcile Iris's "estimated" against the locked completeness enum (1a vs 1b).
  - Decide rename vs schema-bump for delta → delta_percent.
  - Pick the shape of baseline_window (object vs duration + offset).
  - Confirm experimental is per-instance boolean, not a surface synonym.

Once those are settled, the envelope above is the v0 Lantern shape for this event. Say the word and I will draft the runbook entry or update the Lantern architecture doc with the locked fields.

input.body:
Scope: every stop/pause/abort condition for the rollout of bounded queue + backpressure on metrics-router. A single triggered condition halts forward motion until reviewed. "Stop" = freeze advance and page on-call. "Pause" = hold at current canary %, no new traffic shift, no rollback. Severity tier in [S0..S3] is the on-call paging tier when the condition trips.

A. HARD STOP CONDITIONS (page immediately, do not continue rollout)
  A1. [S0] Any data-loss signal: accepted-but-unpersisted counter rises non-zero, or post-rollout replay diverges from pre-rollout golden for any tenant.
  A2. [S0] Backpressure applied to a tenant that is contractually exempted (see exemption list in rollout ticket); one occurrence is enough.
  A3. [S0] Shard-keeper serving goes unready while metrics-router is on the new queue path (cross-service regression; see shard-keeper runbook for cross-check).
  A4. [S0] metrics-router crash-loop (>=3 restarts in 10 min) on the canary cohort.
  A5. [S0] p99 enqueue->ack latency regresses > 2x pre-rollout baseline for > 5 min sustained on the canary cohort.

B. PAUSE-AND-REVIEW CONDITIONS (hold canary %, page on-call for review within 30 min)
  B1. [S1] Queue depth sustained > 80% of bound for > 2 min on any shard (suggests bound is too tight for current load).
  B2. [S1] Backpressure reject rate > 0.5% of accepted requests over any 5-min window on the canary cohort.
  B3. [S1] Any of the four dual-outcome failure modes returns in metrics-router suite: RACE, CRASH (closed 10/11+10/26), DISCONNECT (OPEN — no post-acceptance caller-disconnect regression coverage yet), or a NEW dual-outcome axis. CRASH was closed 2027-10-26 (1 durable id + 1 terminal outcome per accepted attempt, 0 dual). DISCONNECT remains OPEN; any new DISCONNECT hit is a stop, not a pause.
  B4. [S2] Watch-rearm latch misbehaves: rearm reports "success" while freshness is unvouched, or fresh install fails to re-green (per 2027-10-25 metrics-router review closure conditions (a)-(c)).
  B5. [S2] ingest-edge error rate attributable to metrics-router backpressure rises > 0.1% over baseline on the canary cohort.
  B6. [S2] otel-collector drops attributable to metrics-router exceed 0 in any 1-min bucket on the canary cohort.

C. ROLLBACK CONDITIONS (revert to pre-rollout build, do not wait for review)
  C1. [S0] Two or more A-tier conditions trip within a 15-min window.
  C2. [S0] Any single A-tier condition persists > 15 min without clear root cause.
  C3. [S1] Combined B1+B2 sustained > 10 min (queue saturated AND rejecting).
  C4. [S1] Tenant-impacting complaint from a non-canary cohort traced to rollout bleed (config drift, shared resource, sidecar).

D. INVESTIGATE-BEFORE-CONTINUING CONDITIONS (do not auto-halt; flag in rollout channel)
  D1. [S3] Queue-bound headroom < 20% at p99 load on the canary cohort (tight, not failing).
  D2. [S3] Backpressure reject rate between 0.1% and 0.5% over a 5-min window (sub-B2 but trending).
  D3. [S3] Memory or GC pause regression < 2x but > 1.2x baseline on the canary cohort.
  D4. [S3] Canary cohort selection drifts (canary hash bucket share deviates > 2pp from target).

E. GOVERNANCE / PROCESS GATES (block advance to next rollout stage)
  E1. Rollout ticket missing exemption list, rollback runbook link, or on-call escalation path.
  E2. Pre-rollout golden / replay artifact not archived before first canary shift.
  E3. Cross-service impact review with shard-keeper, ingest-edge, and otel-collector not signed off.
  E4. Hema has not been notified of the cutover schedule (metrics migration co-owner; may reorder cutover — reference 2026 collaboration norm).

F. RESUMPTION REQUIREMENTS (any stop/pause must clear all of these before advance)
  F1. Root cause documented in the rollout ticket with a single owner.
  F2. Mitigation merged or revert confirmed clean on the canary cohort.
  F3. Post-mitigation observation window: 30 min for B-tier, 60 min for A-tier, with no re-trigger.
  F4. On-call sign-off recorded in the rollout ticket before the next canary % shift.

Reference: 2027-10-11 metrics-router dual-outcome review (Wes); 2027-10-25 metrics-router watch-rearm review (Wes); 2027-10-26 metrics-router publication-crash review (Wes, 3K crashes → 1 durable id + 1 terminal outcome, CRASH axis closed). DISCONNECT axis remains OPEN — treat any new post-acceptance caller-disconnect regression as A3-equivalent until suite coverage lands.

Severity tiers: S0 page now, S1 page within 5 min, S2 page within 30 min, S3 next business day.

pr.description: The catalog-sync card currently displays `Unknown owner`. This patch adds a static `Product Engineering` owner value to the card configuration so the UI can display an owner immediately.
pr.title: lantern: fill catalog-sync owner in card config

input.body:
Thanks for the unblock. One concern before this lands:

Hard-coding `owner: 'Product Engineering'` replaces a missing real owner with a team name. The UI will stop showing "Unknown owner", but the catalog-sync service still has no named owner in the owner-map. That gap is what the unknown-owner state is signaling — it's a configuration defect, not a display defect.

A couple of concrete risks with this as written:
- When something breaks on catalog-sync, "Product Engineering" doesn't tell the on-caller who to page. It looks assigned without being assigned.
- The card now diverges from the owner-map source of truth. Anyone reconciling cards against the owner-map later will see a permanent mismatch.
- It sets a precedent: any card with a missing owner can be "fixed" by stamping a team label on it, which slowly erodes the signal.

What I'd suggest instead, in rough order of preference:
1. Identify the actual owner for catalog-sync and add them to the owner-map; wire the card to read from there. Then drop the hard-coded line.
2. If we genuinely don't know the owner yet, leave the card reading from the owner-map and accept the "Unknown owner" display until the gap is resolved — i.e. make the unknown state visible, not hidden. That's what surfaces the defect.
3. If a short-term UI fix is needed while we sort out (1), at minimum name the literal human/role accountable, not the team, and link the follow-up issue in the card config or PR description so the placeholder has an expiration.

Happy to talk through who the right owner should be — I don't have context on who actually runs catalog-sync day-to-day.

Also worth flagging since owner-map is in the exclusions for the current Lantern term: any change here needs to land before the next freeze window if we want it in the active bundle, otherwise it'll queue behind the owner-map reference resolution.

temporary tuning knob and the service is not expected to return to the
prior queue shape.

**Observed at 50% and full production:**

- Noisy-tenant tests preserved the eight-waiting cap — a single noisy
  tenant could not push other tenants past the cap.
- Newly queued low-volume tenants entered the ring immediately —
  small or bursty tenants were not stranded behind a dominant noisy
  tenant.
- Work-conserving dispatch used each eligible slot — when eligible
  work existed, slots were not left idle.
- Empty tenants disappeared from the ring after cancellation — the
  ring shed vacated slots rather than holding dead entries.
- Every queue-cap response retained `Retry-After` — clients continued
  to receive a usable back-off signal at the cap.

behavior (do not relax; do not roll a queue change forward without
re-checking each of these against the proposed change):**

- Two-active-per-tenant limit.
- Bounded-decompression requirement.
- Retry requirements (incl. the v2.19.4 randomized 1–3s `Retry-After`

input.body:
Blocking — the patch conflates two different services.

The April 18 outage was a producer/consumer label-name mismatch where:
- shard-keeper (producer) emitted the new label, and

3. If you want a clarifying note, add (not replace) one stating that "metric-rollup" appears nowhere in this incident and should not be conflated with rollup-service.

# Goal
First-cut controls for the Q4 Cardinality Guardrails work; keep it tied to the September mirror/replay legacy-aggregator wobble without turning validation movement into rollback criteria.

# First-cut matrix

## 1. Label limits
- Failure mode: unbounded or newly introduced label keys/values causing fanout.
- Candidate control: a narrow allowlist or budget per sensitive label family.
- Preflight: flag new high-cardinality labels before a metrics-router or shard-keeper push.

## 2. Alert-source semantics
- Failure mode: responders treating replay/mirror validation movement as live-path rollback evidence.
- Candidate control: dashboard and alert wording that marks live metrics-router traffic separately from replay or mirror validation samples.

## 3. Label-change preflight
- Failure mode: a config or parser change adding labels without checking cardinality behavior.
- Candidate control: a pre-push checklist with sample counts, source label, owner, and rollback/non-rollback semantics.

# Non-goals
- No customer-facing dashboard.
- No general telemetry rewrite.
- No legacy-aggregator retirement claim.
- No claim that the 2% replay sample creates immediate storage savings.
- No Q3 incident framing.

# Monday questions
- What cost examples can Cyrus bring by label family?
- Which preflight checks are service-owned by Alex versus data-platform advisory?
- What would make the first cut too broad?

## Bounded observability example — exception-review outcomes

The accepted production counter uses only these bounded labels:
- `service_pair_class`: `ingest_path`, `routing_path`, `ownership_path`, or `other`
- `exception_class`: `invariant`, `provenance`, `failure_mode`, `ownership`, or `escalation`
- `outcome`: `requested`, `accepted`, or `rejected`

Raw service names, owner email addresses, pull-request identifiers, and reviewer-supplied reasons remain in logs or audit records rather than metric labels. This example creates no centralized review owner: mapped owners retain implementation, operational, release, and rollback responsibility, while boundary review remains limited to the triggered cross-service exception.

# INC-2023-10-30-001 metrics-router canary rollback — lightweight after-action

## Summary
A metrics-router canary for `sha:b41c77a` was rolled back after live-path p99 and dropped writes moved on the canary slice. Replay and mirror validation panels were not the rollback trigger.

## Timeline
- 08:07 ET — Page fired for live metrics-router p99 on canary slice. Alex acknowledged the incident.
- 08:22 ET — Live-path p99 was around 118 ms, error rate was 0.18%, and dropped writes were 0.6% on the canary slice. Alex rolled back the most recent metrics-router deploy.
- 09:05 ET — p99 returned to about 46 ms, error rate returned to roughly 0.02%, and dropped writes returned to zero.

## What changed
The canary appears to have changed the `route_pattern` normalization path so one live handler emitted raw account/widget IDs instead of normalized route patterns. Replay validation still showed normalized route patterns, so replay evidence alone would not have caught the live hot-path value-shape change.

## Why rollback was appropriate
The signal was live-path metrics-router movement: p99 and dropped writes on the canary slice. Replay or mirror validation movement remains investigation evidence, not rollback criteria.

## Follow-ups
1. Keep the code fix small: restore normalized `route_pattern` values for the affected live handler before another canary.
2. Patch the Cardinality Guardrails checklist so live-path label value-shape changes require live canary evidence or a representative live-path fixture, not only replay validation.

## Non-goals
This note is not a broad incident postmortem, not a legacy-aggregator retirement discussion, and not a claim that Cardinality Guardrails is complete.

- Participating SDKs reject batches above 8,000 points before transmission.

# Deployed status — May 28, 2026

Product Engineering deployed Lantern PR 1089's tenant-scoped published-service alias resolution for Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce on May 28, 2026.

# Resolution rule

Lantern may resolve a historical service identifier only when the tenant-scoped owner map publishes an alias record containing the old identifier, the canonical published service identifier, and an effective interval covering the source event's timestamp. Both the effective interval's start timestamp and end timestamp are inclusive, so a source event timestamp equal to either endpoint is covered.

If no such record exists, the source event timestamp is earlier than the inclusive start timestamp, or the source event timestamp is later than the inclusive end timestamp, Lantern keeps the signals separate and renders ownership as explicit unknown. The UI does not infer a rename from similar names or customer context.

# Harbor Health result

The original Harbor Health `claims-edge` event now resolves to published `claims-ingest` ownership because its source timestamp is covered by the owner map's published alias interval.

# Regression evidence

Across 28 executed fixtures:
- All 12 valid in-interval aliases joined to their canonical published service identifiers.
- Eight out-of-interval aliases remained separate with explicit unknown ownership.
- Eight identifiers with no published alias record remained separate with explicit unknown ownership.

# Affected safety rerun

Alex's affected safety rerun found no cross-tenant resolution, missing provenance, unpublished ownership render, excluded field, adapter call after denial, or loss of read-only enforcement.

# Approved customer-facing wording

Authorized join: `Published service identity resolved from an owner-map alias effective at this source event timestamp.`

No qualifying alias: `Ownership unknown: no published owner-map alias covers this source event timestamp.`

# Unchanged boundary

The deployment applies only to Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce. It adds no heuristic identity inference and does not expand the customer data contract.

## July 3, 2026 — deployed overlap correction

Lantern now evaluates every tenant-scoped owner-map alias whose inclusive effective interval covers the source event timestamp. If all qualifying records identify the same canonical published service, Lantern resolves that identity once. If qualifying records identify two or more distinct canonical services, Lantern keeps the signals separate and renders ownership as explicit unknown regardless of storage order. Both effective-interval endpoints remain inclusive.

Executed regressions show the overlapping Harbor Health `claims-ingest` and `claims-router` records failing closed in both row orders, both inclusive endpoints working, and a single valid match resolving normally. Alex's affected safety rerun found no cross-tenant resolution, missing provenance, unpublished ownership render, excluded field, adapter call after denial, or loss of read-only enforcement.

The correction is live for Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce. Their two-account read-only scope and customer data contract remain unchanged.

# Q4 incident practice — November 18 scoring sheet

## Scope
A bounded tabletop scoring sheet, not a production runbook. Score observable responder behavior for an accepted metrics-router action across cancellation, caller disconnect, process recovery, and publication.

## Core criteria
1. Durable attempt identity
- Pass: Responders identify the durable acceptance boundary and preserve one attempt identity after acceptance.
- Fail: They create, assume, or accept multiple identities for the same accepted attempt.

2. Terminal accounting
- Pass: Every accepted attempt reaches exactly one terminal result.
- Fail: An accepted attempt has no terminal result or exposes conflicting terminal results.

3. Failure classification
- Pass: Responders distinguish cancellation, caller disconnect, process recovery, and publication using the acceptance boundary.
- Fail: They collapse those cases or treat a pre-acceptance event as evidence about accepted work.

## Wes — responder path
Responders must first determine whether durable acceptance occurred before interpreting cancellation, caller disconnect, process recovery, or publication. After acceptance, they must preserve one durable attempt identity and exactly one terminal result.

## Nadia — postmortem criteria
The postmortem must name the absent system guarantee or control. It must not treat the triggering operator action as the root cause, and it must retain the mapped implementation and rollback owner.

## Final ownership-boundary condition
- Pass: Mapped owners retain implementation and rollback decisions, while the triggered reviewer remains confined to the named failure-mode boundary.
- Fail: The triggered review is treated as implementation, release, or rollback approval.

## Additional operating checks — November 8

### 45-minute secondary boundary
- Pass: When the cause remains unisolated, responders engage the secondary before the 45-minute boundary and make the incident clock visible.
- Fail: Responders wait until or after 45 minutes, or continue without engaging the secondary while the cause remains unisolated.

### Friday staging preparation versus production change
- Pass: Responders identify staging preparation that makes no production state change as staging work and separately identify a Friday-afternoon production deploy as prohibited.
- Fail: Responders classify staging-only preparation as a production deploy, or permit a Friday-afternoon production state change because it was described as preparation.

These checks supplement the accepted cancellation, caller-disconnect, durable-attempt, terminal-result, mapped-owner, and postmortem criteria. This remains a tabletop scoring sheet rather than a production runbook.

## November 18 execution order

- 5 minutes: role and ownership framing.
- 35 minutes: cancellation and caller-disconnect scenario.
- 10 minutes: one targeted rerun if a scoring boundary is missed.
- 10 minutes: debrief and owner follow-up.

Wes teaches the responder path. Nadia owns the postmortem section. Alex maintains only the bounded failure case. This is the exact one-hour tabletop sequence and does not turn the scoring sheet into a production runbook.

## Observed results — November 18

The tabletop is complete. Responders correctly separated durable acceptance from cancellation, caller disconnect, and process recovery; preserved one attempt identity and one terminal result in the exercise; identified Wes as the mapped metrics-router implementation, release, and rollback owner; and distinguished Friday staging preparation from a production change.

The first run engaged the secondary at minute 47 while the cause remained unisolated, missing the required before-45-minute boundary. The targeted rerun engaged the secondary at minute 42 and passed that boundary. Nadia’s debrief named the missing system control rather than the triggering operator action as root cause.

These results are training evidence only. The tabletop did not execute the product implementation and does not close any product defect or replace required executable product evidence.

arguments.body:
# Q1 2027 platform workstreams — Lantern, Guardrails, and owner map

Owner of this document: Alex (reviewer role: shared-contract and failure-boundary).
Status as of 2027-02-05: living document. Sections below reflect the December 17
final decision, the December 28 kickoff-prep framing, the December 29 participant
proposals, the January 11 staff-only rehearsal acceptance checklist, the January 22
Q1 joint handoff rehearsal result (M–P), the February 4 source-side correction
(Cyrus republish of 2 Cardinality Guardrails records), the February 4 wording close
(Iris on the corrected staff-only reference slice), and the February 5–18 internal
operating observation (Q–S). Nothing here authorizes customer exposure or transfers
routine implementation ownership to Alex.

================================================================
1. APPROVED SPLIT (unchanged from December 17 review)
================================================================

Q1 2027 is three linked workstreams, not one Lantern monolith:

  - Lantern          — owns explanation and navigation. Reference-only.
  - Cardinality      — owns pipeline limits and cost semantics (authoritative).
    Guardrails
  - Owner map        — owns published responsibility (authoritative).

Lantern implementation is owned by Product Engineering. Alex is not the routine
implementation gate for any of the three workstreams. Alex reviews the shared
five-field contract and the cross-system failure boundaries only.

Lantern does not absorb owner-map data or Cardinality Guardrails data. Lantern
does not write into published responsibility. Lantern does not place limit or
cost data on a customer surface.

================================================================
2. FIVE-FIELD SHARED REFERENCE CONTRACT
================================================================

Per the December 17 review, internal Lantern cards may navigate staff to
authoritative owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails records using ONLY these
five fields — no others:

  1. tenant_id
  2. canonical_service_id
  3. authority_type
  4. authority_record_id
  5. source_timestamp

Rules of use:
  - Each reference carries exactly these five fields and nothing more.
  - Owner-map references and Cardinality Guardrails references carry
    SEPARATE authority identities and SEPARATE source timestamps — they
    are not collapsed into one reference and never share an
    authority_record_id.
  - If an authority record is stale (source_timestamp older than the
    freshness threshold for that authority_type) or missing (no current
    authority_record_id), Lantern MUST render the reference as explicit
    "unknown" with the stale/missing field shown — it does NOT guess,
    default, copy from cache, or fall back to a payload value.
  - Lantern MUST NOT copy any authority payload value into the card.
  - Lantern MUST NOT offer mutation capability into either authority.
  - On a denial (stale, missing, or out-of-scope), Lantern MUST NOT issue
    any adapter call afterwards. Zero adapter calls after denial.
  - These rules apply equally to staff-only and internal-shadow surfaces.

================================================================
3. JANUARY 22 STAFF-ONLY REHEARSAL — ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST
================================================================

Rehearsal date: 2027-01-22. Audience: staff only. Purpose: dry-run the
internal operating use of Lantern references against live authority records,
under the December 17 rules. The rehearsal is NOT a customer-exposure
authorization and is NOT a transfer of routine implementation ownership to
Alex. Product Engineering remains the implementation owner for the rehearsal
slice. Alex reviews whether the slice meets this checklist.

Pass criteria — every item MUST hold. A single failure blocks "passed."

  [A] Reference shape
      A.1  Every Lantern reference emitted during the rehearsal carries
           ONLY tenant_id, canonical_service_id, authority_type,
           authority_record_id, and source_timestamp.
      A.2  No reference carries any additional field, annotation, payload
           value, computed derivation, or display string derived from the
           authority payload.

  [B] Separate identities and source timestamps
      B.1  Every owner-map reference carries its own authority_record_id
           and its own source_timestamp.
      B.2  Every Cardinality Guardrails reference carries its own
           authority_record_id and its own source_timestamp.
      B.3  No reference shares an authority_record_id between owner-map
           and Cardinality Guardrails.
      B.4  No reference collapses the two authorities into a single
           combined reference.

  [C] Stale or missing authority records
      C.1  A reference whose source_timestamp is older than the freshness
           threshold for its authority_type is rendered as EXPLICIT
           "unknown — stale authority_record" with the
           authority_record_id and source_timestamp still shown (no
           hiding, no caching past the value).
      C.2  A reference with no current authority_record_id is rendered as
           EXPLICIT "unknown — no current authority_record" with
           tenant_id and canonical_service_id still shown.
      C.3  No reference defaults, fabricates, or back-fills a missing or
           stale authority_record_id.

  [D] Zero adapter calls after denial
      D.1  After a denial (stale, missing, out-of-scope, or unsupported
           authority_type), the rehearsal slice makes ZERO adapter calls
           to the owner-map system or to Cardinality Guardrails for the
           same (tenant_id, canonical_service_id) pair.
      D.2  Adapter-call counts before vs. after denial are recorded in
           the rehearsal evidence; the post-denial count is exactly zero.

  [E] No payload copy, no mutation path
      E.1  No Lantern card in the rehearsal displays a copied authority
           payload value (no copied limit value, no copied cost value,
           no copied published-responsibility text).
      E.2  No Lantern card in the rehearsal exposes or links to a
           mutation path into the owner map or into Cardinality
           Guardrails.

  [F] No Harbor Health or Mosaic Commerce surface
      F.1  No authority payload value, mutation path, or customer-path
           request, artifact, or output for Harbor Health is produced,
           referenced, copied, or implied by the rehearsal.
      F.2  No authority payload value, mutation path, or customer-path
           request, artifact, or output for Mosaic Commerce is produced,
           referenced, copied, or implied by the rehearsal.
      F.3  Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce remain absent from the
           rehearsal surface exactly as they were absent on December 17.

  [G] Boundary preservation
      G.1  Lantern remains the explanation and navigation layer; it does
           not become authoritative for pipeline limits, cost semantics,
           or published responsibility.
      G.2  Cardinality Guardrails remains authoritative for pipeline
           limits and cost semantics.
      G.3  The owner map remains authoritative for published
           responsibility.
      G.4  Product Engineering remains the implementation owner of the
           Lantern rehearsal slice; Alex does not become the routine

pr.author: roman
pr.description: Ships a metrics-router check that rejects changes exceeding the configured label-count ceiling. The PR describes this as the complete first-release control slice; all validation beyond the metrics-router label-count check is deferred to future work.

input.body:
The label-count ceiling is a real and useful cardinality control, and the scope of this PR (one validator plus unit tests on the metrics-router change path) is appropriately narrow. What I can't approve is the claim that this is the complete first-release control slice.

A first-release cardinality control slice, as I understand it, needs to address both standard cardinality vectors, not just one:

  1. Label count - covered by this PR.
  2. Label-value cardinality - not covered. This is the dominant cardinality incident vector in practice (a user_id, request_id, or high-resolution timestamp label blowing up series counts under a low label count). A 3-label metric with unbounded label values is still unbounded cardinality; the label-count ceiling alone doesn't reach it.

In addition, the cap source is unclear. Cardinality Guardrails owns pipeline limits and cost semantics as the authoritative source (per the Q1 platform-workstreams doc, sections around Cardinality Guardrails as the limit/cost-semantics authority), and the project norm is for the metrics-router to consume those limits via Cardinality Guardrails rather than carry hardcoded values. If the label-count ceiling here is hardcoded in metrics-router, that is itself a layering question for the slice claim: the budget authority lives in Cardinality Guardrails and is not touched by this PR.

The branch name (first-release-label-counts) and your own description ("all validation beyond the metrics-router label-count check is deferred to future work") both signal this PR is the label-counts *part* of the slice, not the whole slice. The PR title overstates what the diff delivers.

Suggested path:
  - Land this PR as the label-counts piece - the validator and tests look clean and worth keeping.
  - Open a follow-on (or expand this branch) to add at least the label-value cardinality control and the Cardinality Guardrails budget wiring before claiming "complete first-release control slice."
  - Happy to revise this review if "first-release control slice" has a tighter, pre-agreed scope definition I am missing - point me at the source and I will re-check.

tests.answer:
Inspection result for metrics-validation#913

Author: roman
Branch: roman/legacy-mirror-required-source
Opened: 2027-12-30
Status: open; alex is reviewer, roman is assignee
Title: "metrics-validation: require legacy mirror when OTel validation is unstable"

Proposed changes (per PR body):
  1. Adds the legacy mirror to required validation sources.
  2. Allows mirror output to satisfy validation when the OTel test fails.
  3. Quarantines the intermittently failing OTel test without changing its fixtures.
Reported checks: otel_validation=intermittent failure, legacy_mirror_validation=passing.

Review of the proposed response

The quarantine of the flaky OTel test (item 3) is a reasonable short-term action on its own, but items 1 and 2 should not ship as described. Combined, they re-introduce the dual-source-of-truth failure mode the metrics-router 10/11 boundary review was specifically closed against.

Concrete problems with the proposal:

  a. Dual-outcome validation. "Allows mirror output to satisfy validation when the OTel test fails" means the suite accepts a pass from either source. When OTel and the mirror disagree, the suite no longer detects the disagreement — it picks whichever passes and reports green. This is structurally the same anti-pattern as the metrics-router cancel-vs-publish dual-outcome bug (10/11 review, closure: one durable id + one terminal outcome per accepted attempt; closed again on 10/26 with 0 dual across 3K crash spans). Validation that "satisfies" on either of two sources cannot be a single-source-of-truth gate, and silently endorsing one of two inconsistent answers is exactly what the metrics pipeline is no longer allowed to do.

  b. Re-requiring the legacy mirror as a required source. The mirror was moved off the required path for the same reason: a required secondary source lets the suite pass when the primary diverges. Promoting it back to required, even with the stated OTel-unavailability fallback, recreates that bypass. If the goal is resilience to OTel outages, the correct shape is: OTel is the authoritative source; mirror is an observability/debug aid that is compared against OTel and must agree when both run — never a substitute for an OTel pass.

  c. Untargeted quarantine. Quarantining the flaky test without changing its fixtures and without an exit criterion ("collect more runs" is not a criterion) does not converge. A quarantine needs: (i) a tracked owner and exit threshold (e.g. N consecutive passes after the suspected fix), (ii) a deadline for either fix or removal from the suite, and (iii) the fixture/test under investigation so the run history is reproducible. Without these, the test sits in quarantine indefinitely and the fallback in (b) becomes permanent by default.

  d. No root-cause signal. "Intermittent failure" is a symptom, not a finding. The proposal makes the suite green in spite of the symptom rather than characterizing it (rate, correlation with env/PR/load, last-N history). Without that, neither the quarantine exit nor the decision to keep the mirror around is grounded.

Recommended response

  - Land a minimal quarantine-only change for the flaky OTel test, with: explicit exit criterion (consecutive-pass count and/or wall-clock deadline), owner, and a tracking issue id referenced in the test marker and in the PR description. No fixture changes unless root-caused.
  - Reject items 1 and 2 of the current PR. The legacy mirror must not be a required validation source, and mirror output must not satisfy validation in OTel's place. If disagreement detection between OTel and the mirror is desired, that is a separate, additive check that fails the suite on divergence — it does not paper over it.
  - Open a follow-up to characterize the intermittent failure (last-N runs, environmental correlation, suspected cause) so the quarantine has a path to closure rather than an open-ended "more runs".

Net recommendation: request_changes on this PR as written. The quarantine framing is right; the mirror-as-fallback framing is the same failure_mode class as the metrics-router dual-outcome boundary and should not be re-introduced in the validation suite.

Ready to submit this as a formal review on metrics-validation#913 if you want it filed via review_pr (decision=request_changes). Let me know and I'll send it.

tests.request: Inspect otel-schema#411 and review its production deployment.environment changes for normalization, missing input, invalid input, per-tenant cardinality, and three-service parity.

pr.author: mira
pr.description: Change deployment.environment processing so every supplied string is lowercased and published. Missing input is published as unknown, qa is treated as valid, and the per-tenant distinct-value limiter is removed.
pr.diff_summary: Replaces the deployment.environment allowlist with generic lowercase normalization; emits unknown for absent input; adds qa fixtures; removes the three-value tenant cap.
pr.title: otel-schema: broaden deployment.environment values

input.body:
Reviewing the four dimensions. Card is request_changes — three concrete blockers (cardinality cap removal without replacement, sentinel collision, empty-string handling) plus a parity coordination gap.

Normalization
- Lowercase-only is consistent with itself, but there's no trim and no internal-whitespace handling. " dev ", "dev\t", "dev\n" each become distinct post-lowercase values and will leak straight through to the metric backend. Recommend trim-then-lowercase, and either reject or collapse internal whitespace. Pure case-fold is fine for the ASCII set we use; if you want to be defensive about Unicode, say so explicitly in the schema doc rather than relying on the runtime's default fold.

Missing input → "unknown"
- The sentinel "unknown" is itself a valid input value. A tenant that legitimately has an environment named "unknown" becomes indistinguishable from a span/metric with no environment attribute. This hurts debuggability (the exact case the previous allowlist was meant to keep clean). Recommend reserving a sentinel that can't collide with normal input, e.g., always re-map any user-supplied "unknown" to a distinct reserved form, or use a different reserved token ("_missing", "<unset>"). Either way, the reserved token must be documented as reserved so tenants don't adopt it.
- Empty string and whitespace-only string should also map to missing. Currently "" lowercases to "" and is published as a distinct value — that's neither "missing" nor a real environment.

Invalid input
- There is no invalid input anymore. Every typo, hostname, branch name, container ID, or build SHA that someone mistakenly stuffs into deployment.environment is published verbatim (modulo lowercase). Previously the allowlist + cap caught this; now nothing does. This is the load-bearing risk of the change and it's not mitigated.

Per-tenant cardinality
- Removing the three-value cap entirely removes the only safety mechanism against the previous bullet. A single misconfigured tenant publishing N typos / branch names / laptop hostnames over time creates N unbounded distinct values, and cardinality in the metric backend is global — one tenant's explosion degrades the platform for everyone.
- Recommend one of: (a) raise the cap (e.g., 10–25) rather than remove it, (b) keep a per-tenant LRU with eviction and add a per-tenant alert at ~50% of the cap so we hear about misconfigs before they cost us, (c) scope the relaxation: whitelist the small set of additional env values you actually need to support (qa plus the named customer environments) and leave the rest of the allowlist in place. Option (c) is the smallest delta from current behavior and the easiest to reason about; the description doesn't tell me which option you intend, and "removed" is the wrong default.

Three-service parity
- otel-schema defines the contract; ingest-edge, shard-keeper, and metrics-router consume it. The PR list shows only this PR — no companion changes are visible. If those three services aren't updated in the same release window, we get a desync window where producers emit lowercase + "unknown" + uncapped values and consumers still enforce the old allowlist/cap, which means silent label stripping or drops and dashboards that go blank mid-cutover.
- Please link the companion PRs (or branch names) for ingest-edge, shard-keeper, and metrics-router before merge, and confirm a coordinated cutover — schema and consumers in the same release, with the consumer changes landed first behind a feature flag if you want to stage it. I'm the owner on metrics-router side; happy to coordinate the change there once the final semantics are nailed down (especially the missing-input sentinel and whether the cap is removed vs raised).

Test coverage gaps (per diff_summary)
- No mention of tests for: empty/whitespace-only input, mixed-case input, the "unknown" sentinel collision, the cap-removal behavior under a misconfigured tenant, or end-to-end parity across the three consumers. At minimum I want fixtures for the first four before merge.

Rollout / observability
- Once this lands, every previously-missing deployment.environment will start emitting "unknown" (or whatever sentinel is chosen). Capture a pre-merge baseline of "spans/metrics with no deployment.environment" per tenant so we can validate post-merge that the new "unknown" volume matches and isn't absorbing garbage from a typo'd real env.

Blocking on: (1) cap removal vs raise vs whitelist decision, (2) sentinel collision resolution, (3) empty-string handling, (4) companion-PR links for the three consumers.

Review submitted: request_changes on otel-schema#411, review id review_cbb4875a1ae34482b180a56bc0229c0a.

What I covered:

checks.observed:
Reviewing the four dimensions. Card is request_changes — three concrete blockers (cardinality cap removal without replacement, sentinel collision, empty-string handling) plus a parity coordination gap.

Normalization
- Lowercase-only is consistent with itself, but there's no trim and no internal-whitespace handling. " dev ", "dev\t", "dev\n" each become distinct post-lowercase values and will leak straight through to the metric backend. Recommend trim-then-lowercase, and either reject or collapse internal whitespace. Pure case-fold is fine for the ASCII set we use; if you want to be defensive about Unicode, say so explicitly in the schema doc rather than relying on the runtime's default fold.

Missing input → "unknown"
- The sentinel "unknown" is itself a valid input value. A tenant that legitimately has an environment named "unknown" becomes indistinguishable from a span/metric with no environment attribute. This hurts debuggability (the exact case the previous allowlist was meant to keep clean). Recommend reserving a sentinel that can't collide with normal input, e.g., always re-map any user-supplied "unknown" to a distinct reserved form, or use a different reserved token ("_missing", "<unset>"). Either way, the reserved token must be documented as reserved so tenants don't adopt it.
- Empty string and whitespace-only string should also map to missing. Currently "" lowercases to "" and is published as a distinct value — that's neither "missing" nor a real environment.

Invalid input
- There is no invalid input anymore. Every typo, hostname, branch name, container ID, or build SHA that someone mistakenly stuffs into deployment.environment is published verbatim (modulo lowercase). Previously the allowlist + cap caught this; now nothing does. This is the load-bearing risk of the change and it's not mitigated.

Per-tenant cardinality
- Removing the three-value cap entirely removes the only safety mechanism against the previous bullet. A single misconfigured tenant publishing N typos / branch names / laptop hostnames over time creates N unbounded distinct values, and cardinality in the metric backend is global — one tenant's explosion degrades the platform for everyone.
- Recommend one of: (a) raise the cap (e.g., 10–25) rather than remove it, (b) keep a per-tenant LRU with eviction and add a per-tenant alert at ~50% of the cap so we hear about misconfigs before they cost us, (c) scope the relaxation: whitelist the small set of additional env values you actually need to support (qa plus the named customer environments) and leave the rest of the allowlist in place. Option (c) is the smallest delta from current behavior and the easiest to reason about; the description doesn't tell me which option you intend, and "removed" is the wrong default.

Three-service parity
- otel-schema defines the contract; ingest-edge, shard-keeper, and metrics-router consume it. The PR list shows only this PR — no companion changes are visible. If those three services aren't updated in the same release window, we get a desync window where producers emit lowercase + "unknown" + uncapped values and consumers still enforce the old allowlist/cap, which means silent label stripping or drops and dashboards that go blank mid-cutover.
- Please link the companion PRs (or branch names) for ingest-edge, shard-keeper, and metrics-router before merge, and confirm a coordinated cutover — schema and consumers in the same release, with the consumer changes landed first behind a feature flag if you want to stage it. I'm the owner on metrics-router side; happy to coordinate the change there once the final semantics are nailed down (especially the missing-input sentinel and whether the cap is removed vs raised).

Test coverage gaps (per diff_summary)
- No mention of tests for: empty/whitespace-only input, mixed-case input, the "unknown" sentinel collision, the cap-removal behavior under a misconfigured tenant, or end-to-end parity across the three consumers. At minimum I want fixtures for the first four before merge.

Rollout / observability
- Once this lands, every previously-missing deployment.environment will start emitting "unknown" (or whatever sentinel is chosen). Capture a pre-merge baseline of "spans/metrics with no deployment.environment" per tenant so we can validate post-merge that the new "unknown" volume matches and isn't absorbing garbage from a typo'd real env.

Blocking on: (1) cap removal vs raise vs whitelist decision, (2) sentinel collision resolution, (3) empty-string handling, (4) companion-PR links for the three consumers.
