arguments.body:
# Lantern platform boundary proposal — March 26 strategy review

Author: Alex Valdez
Date: 2026-02-19
Reviewers at the March 26 strategy decision: Hema, Theo, Iris, Alex
Companion to: Lantern post-March questions — working session (2026-02-19 with Iris)
Origin: Two customer requests (Harbor Health release-readiness label; Mosaic Commerce per-service cost context)

## What this document is

The agreed architecture and responsibility split produced from the 2026-02-19 working session with Iris, taken together with the final Mosaic continuation evidence, for the strategy decision Hema has scheduled for March 26, 2026, 10:30–11:30 AM.

## Customer requests under discussion

1. Harbor Health — release-readiness label (a human-performance / go-decision judgment layered on Lantern output).
2. Mosaic Commerce — per-service cost context surfaced to customers (a cost attribution signal layered on Cardinality Guardrails output).

## Agreed architecture and responsibility split

- Lantern — provenance-backed service and system state. Lantern answers "what does this source say about this entity, and when did it say it." Lantern does not generate release-readiness judgments or human-performance interpretations, and does not emit cost attribution.
- Cardinality Guardrails — remains the source for pipeline limits and cost signals. Per-tenant and global pipeline caps, refusal semantics, and cost context originate here. Customer-facing cost context stays under Cardinality Guardrails ownership.
- Owner map — remains the source of published responsibility. The mapping from published_service_id to accountable owner team, on-call rotation, and support channel is owned by the owner map. Lantern consumes it; Lantern does not redefine it.
- Lantern does not absorb Cardinality Guardrails' cost-signal ownership or the owner map's responsibility mapping. Cardinality Guardrails does not absorb Lantern's provenance ownership. The owner map does not absorb either.

## What Lantern is and is not

- Is: a consumer of registered sources that surfaces what each source claims, with provenance (which source), source timestamps (when it was said), and explicit "unknown" for stale or missing input.
- Is not: a system that decides whether a release is ready, that interprets human or team performance, or that publishes cost attribution.
- Is not: a free-form extension point. Every new source type must enter through shared registration (see Registration gate below).

## Registration gate for any new source type

Before any new source type is read by Lantern, all of the following must hold. These are conditions on registration, not on individual reads, and they exist so that Lantern's customer-facing output cannot bypass them.

1. Tenant-scoped authorization before source access — registration must declare which tenants are authorized and the registration must be enforced before any read of that source type against any tenant. A source that is not authorized for a tenant must be unreachable for that tenant.
2. Required provenance and source timestamps — registration must require each record to carry a provenance identifier and a source timestamp. Records missing either are rejected at registration time, not silently coerced at read time.
3. Explicit unknown for stale or missing input — registration must declare staleness bounds and missing-field policy. Reads outside the bounds, or over missing fields, must return explicit "unknown" rather than a derived or imputed value.
4. Excluded-field checks — registration must declare which fields the source type must not carry into Lantern (for example, fields that encode human-performance judgments or cost attribution). Reads that surface an excluded field must be rejected, not redacted silently downstream.
5. Successful safety rerun before customer use — registration is not complete until the shared safety suite has been rerun against the new source type and passed. The safety suite covers authorization enforcement, provenance/timestamp presence, unknown-not-imputation, and excluded-field rejection.

## What this proposal does and does not decide

- Does not decide Lantern's later direction. The March 26 strategy decision is a decision on the proposal as written; it does not lock in subsequent Lantern scope, ownership changes, or roadmap.
- Does not authorize either requested capability. Approval of this proposal does not approve the Harbor Health release-readiness label or the Mosaic Commerce per-service cost context. Each of those remains a separate decision.
- Does not change Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce's existing two-account read-only authorization through March 31, 2026. The current read-only scope for those two accounts continues unchanged until March 31, 2026 regardless of the outcome of the March 26 decision.

## Companion evidence

- Mosaic capacity response — final closeout (doc_1d054bf3238f4d44a691bb7e56c09937, folder: mosaic): 2026-01-08 90-minute staged replay at 19.78M data points per minute qualified; 2026-01-20 production observation at 17.2M data points per minute passed; cycle closed without additional queue design, configuration change, or production push. Forward gate for any forecast above 17.2M data points per minute is preserved.
- Lantern post-March questions — working session (2026-02-19 13:00–14:00 ET, with Iris): produced this proposal.

pr.author: rhea
pr.body:
## Rationale
The October 2025 Mosaic production observation proves that the existing tenant-bounded control lost accepted work under load. The retryable queue-full responses are evidence that accepted batches were discarded once tenants reached the pending-batch ceiling. We should therefore allow substantially more pending work per tenant and remove the global aggregate cap.

## Changes
- Raise `max_pending_batches_per_tenant` to 256.
- Delete `GLOBAL_PENDING_BATCH_LIMIT` and the corresponding aggregate admission check.
- Retain the existing retry response for the remaining per-tenant refusal path.

## Expected effect
Large tenants can accumulate more pending batches without encountering the current queue-full behavior, and aggregate queue capacity is no longer constrained by a process-wide constant.
pr.title: metrics-router: raise tenant pending-batch limit and remove global queue cap

The "October 2025 Mosaic production observation" Rhea cites is the 2025-10-06 watch at 16.0M pts/min and the broader Mosaic scale-response cycle. Both pieces of evidence contradict Rhea's premise:

  - The 2025-10-06 observation recorded q_wait_p99 286 ms, retry_q_full 0.11%, no tenant exceeded 64 pending batches, and no accepted points lost. Critically, the watch explicitly did NOT establish whether any accepted batch was lost (it recorded accepted points, not accepted batches) — that was a scope-of-evidence distinction added at the time.
  - The restart-during-requeue evidence (Wes + Nadia, 2025-11-17, 25,000 injected crash-and-restart runs) qualified the metrics-router accepted-batch diagnostic for prospective production observation and explicitly did NOT retroactively establish whether any accepted batch was lost on 2025-10-06.
  - The 2026-01-08 90-minute staged replay at 19.78M pts/min qualified: q_wait_p99 319 ms, retry_q_full 0.17%, highest tenant 62 pending, every accepted batch reconciled to exactly one terminal result, no accepted batch lost, every cross-service invariant at baseline.
  - The 2026-01-20 production observation at 17.2M pts/min passed: q_wait_p99 302 ms, retry_q_full 0.14%, highest tenant 60 pending, every accepted batch reconciled to exactly one terminal result, no accepted batch lost, every cross-service invariant at baseline.

Did the completed cycle authorize another queue design or configuration change?

No. The 2026-01-22 mapped-group evidence review (Hema, Wes, Cyrus, Roman, Nadia, Alex) closed the Mosaic scale-response cycle and the explicit recorded outcomes were:

  - Mosaic scale-response cycle is CLOSED.
  - No additional queue design, configuration change, or production push.
  - No capacity-related production window remains open.
  - Production control unchanged: global queue 2,048 batches; per-tenant limit 64 pending batches; retryable pre-acceptance backpressure for excess work.
  - Forward gate for any forecast above 17.2M pts/min is preserved: a fresh 90-minute replay at 15% above the new peak, using its tenant/batch-size/burst distribution, qualifies only if all of the same 5-minute stops (q_wait_p99 ≤ 400 ms, retry_q_full ≤ 0.5%), the same per-tenant limit (≤ 64 pending), no accepted-batch loss, and every cross-service invariant at baseline.

So PR #1318 is not authorized. The cycle's stated closeout explicitly preserved the existing control; it did not open a path to raise the per-tenant ceiling or remove the global aggregate cap.

Which queue controls remain in force

From the 2026-01-22 closeout (carried forward unchanged):

  - GLOBAL_PENDING_BATCH_LIMIT: 2,048 batches.
  - MAX_PENDING_BATCHES_PER_TENANT: 64.
  - Backpressure model: retryable pre-acceptance refusal for excess work.
  - Raw accepted_batch_id and transport-attempt identities stay out of metric labels; pre-acceptance refusals stay outside the accepted-batch population.
  - 5-minute stop conditions: q_wait_p99 > 400 ms (cause); retry_q_full > 0.005 (symptom); any accepted-batch loss; baseline departure on consistency / parity / dropped-series / route / shard-keeper lease / rollup-service / full-health.
  - Nadia's alert v2 (q_wait_p99{src}>400 cause, retry_q_full{src}>0.005 symptom, 5-min window, src ∈ {live_prod, staged, replay}, halts active stage, live_prod pages) — historically not live in prod; status not refreshed in the material I can reach.

Review recommendation (grounded)

Reject the PR as submitted. The premise is wrong against the documented evidence base, and the proposed change goes beyond anything the closed cycle authorized. Three specific issues:

  1. Premise contradicted by recorded evidence. Every accepted-batch observation from the cycle (the 2025-11-17 diagnostic qualification, the 2026-01-08 qualifying replay, the 2026-01-20 production observation) reconciled every accepted batch to exactly one terminal result with none lost. The retry_q_full rate during the heaviest qualifying run was 0.17%, well under the 0.5% stop. The 2025-10-06 watch never established that any accepted batch was lost. There is no recorded production evidence of accepted-batch loss under the tenant-bounded control.
  2. Beyond the cycle's authorization. The 2026-01-22 closeout explicitly retained the global queue 2,048 / per-tenant 64 control and stated "no additional queue design, configuration change, or production push." Raising MAX_PENDING_BATCHES_PER_TENANT to 256 and deleting GLOBAL_PENDING_BATCH_LIMIT is exactly the kind of queue design and configuration change the closed cycle did not authorize.
  3. Removal of the global cap is a structural change with no qualifying evidence. The forward gate that authorizes future changes requires a fresh 90-minute replay at 15% above the new forecast peak, with the same stop conditions and cross-service invariants. No such replay has been run for the 256 / no-global-cap design.

If Rhea has new evidence (an accepted-batch loss that the diagnostic missed, or load-test data showing the current control fails a forecast above 17.2M), the right path is to surface that evidence first, then run the forward gate. The PR as written should not be merged.

Note: I did not find a session in this profile where Alex actually filed a review on PR #1318. The PR itself (open, reviewer: Alex, assignee: Rhea, opened 2027-12-29) was retrieved directly from the PR store. All evidence above is grounded in the Mosaic closeout doc `doc_1d054bf3238f4d44a691bb7e56c09937` (folder: mosaic) and the calendar event `evt_08f3e765b189423aa6e3f426ba4cdd9d` recording the 2026-01-22 mapped-group review. bookend_start.content: [2024-11-30T15:30:00-05:00] After the first sidewalk salting of the season, I saw visible salt granules on parts of Kibo's quieter side-street loop. He has no limp, cracked pads, redness, or licking. I want to prevent irritation without abandoning the quieter route. I have lukewarm water, clean towels, and plain pet paw balm, but no booties that fit yet. Give me a pre-walk, route, paw-cleaning, and monitoring plan, including signs that should end the walk or prompt veterinary advice.

PRE-WALK
- Apply paw balm 5-10 min before leaving: thin layer on all 4 pads + between toes. Time to absorb = better barrier.
- Visual scan of stoop and first ½ block. If heavy granules piled at the curb, skip that segment and take an untreated parallel block where one exists.

arguments.body:
# Oversized-batch handling (v2) — Decision and rollout through 2025-01-28

Date of decision: 2025-01-14
Owners: SDK (participating clients) + ingest-edge
Status: Decision LOCKED. Enablement staged through 2025-01-28. Rollout NOT complete.

## 1. Decision summary

After reviewing the completed replay, current- and older-client compatibility results, and the corrected SDK error text, the responsible owners selected the layered permanent oversized-batch design:

- Participating SDKs reject batches above 8,000 points BEFORE transmission and tell the caller to split them.
- ingest-edge retains deterministic HTTP 413 whole-batch rejection for older or nonconforming clients, with:
  - accepted points = 0
  - rejected points = submitted count
  - reason = `oversized_batch`
- The design is permanent (not a temporary cap), and is layered across client and server.

## 2. Inputs the owners reviewed

- Completed replay of the oversized-batch handling changes.
- Current-client compatibility results.
- Older-client compatibility results.
- Corrected SDK error text (post-replay wording fix).

## 3. Selected behavior (specification)

### 3.1 Client (participating SDKs)

- Pre-transmission check: if batch size > 8,000 points, reject locally.
- Caller-facing instruction: "split the batch and retry with smaller batches."
- No HTTP request is issued for the oversized batch.
- No client-side retry of the oversized batch itself.

### 3.2 Server (ingest-edge)

- Receives a batch that exceeds the cap from an older or nonconforming client.
- Response: HTTP 413 (whole-batch rejection — no partial acceptance).
- Counters on the rejected request:
  - accepted = 0
  - rejected = submitted_count
  - reason = `oversized_batch`
- Behavior is deterministic and identical to the replay-validated contract.

### 3.3 Layering rationale (permanent)

- New clients get a fast, clear failure path with no network cost.
- Older / nonconforming clients continue to get a deterministic, well-countered 413 at the edge.
- Both paths emit the same `oversized_batch` reason and identical counter semantics, so observability and accounting converge.

## 4. Stop checks (must hold during enablement through 2025-01-28)

These checks must remain true as each stage turns on. If any check fails, halt the rollout and revert the in-progress stage.

1. Unchanged-retry check: client-side retry behavior on NON-oversized batches is unchanged. Oversized batches are not auto-retried by the client; smaller follow-up batches must succeed normally.
2. Accounting check:
   - For oversized batches: accepted = 0, rejected = submitted_count, reason = `oversized_batch` (every request, every region).
   - For in-limit batches: counters and accounting are unchanged from the pre-rollout baseline.
   - No new drift between client-reported and ingest-edge-reported batch sizes.

## 5. Rollout plan through 2025-01-28

- Enablement is staged, not a single big-bang cutover.
- Window: 2025-01-14 through 2025-01-28.
- Per stage (each participating SDK + ingest-edge slice):
  - Turn on the new pre-transmission check (client) and/or the retained 413 contract (server).
  - Verify the two stop checks above against the staged traffic.
  - Record results before proceeding to the next stage.
- Cutover is considered COMPLETE only when:
  - All participating SDKs have shipped the pre-transmission rejection.
  - ingest-edge is confirmed on the permanent 413 contract across all regions.
  - Both stop checks have held across the full window.

## 6. Open items

- Rollout is not complete as of 2025-01-14. Per-stage results (which SDKs are on, which ingest-edge regions are on, stop-check deltas) to be appended as enablement proceeds through 2025-01-28.
- Older-client behavior confirmed via the replay; no further contract change expected unless a stage surfaces one.
- Corrected SDK error text is the authoritative caller-facing wording for "split and retry smaller batches."

## 7. References

- Replay results (reviewed 2025-01-14).
- Current-client compatibility report (reviewed 2025-01-14).
- Older-client compatibility report (reviewed 2025-01-14).
- Corrected SDK error text (reviewed 2025-01-14).
- Existing oversized-batch v2 contract: 413 + counters (accepted=0, rejected=submitted) + `oversized_batch` + client-no-retry.

Batches with 7,999 points are accepted; 8,000 points are rejected locally; and 8,001 points are rejected locally. Rejected cases make zero network sends.

Acknowledged. Restating to confirm the boundary behavior:

- Validator: `pointCount >= 8000` → reject locally
- 7,999 → accepted
- 8,000, 8,001, anything ≥ 8,000 → rejected locally, zero network sends

That is internally consistent and fail-closed. Two small things worth pinning while this is the active gate:

1. Inclusive reject boundary — 7,999/8,000 is a clean off-by-one probe; if anything ever drifts to `>` or to a different constant, that pair is the canary.
2. Local reject + zero sends means no server-side partial state to clean up, but it also means oversized batches are silently dropped at the SDK. Make sure the staged-enablement telemetry counts rejections and the rejected point total, not just successful sends — otherwise the rollout will look healthier than it is.

Is 8,000 the staged-enablement-only cap (expected to move as the cohort grows) or the intended permanent max? Worth labeling on the staged-enablement doc so it isn't read as the long-term limit later.

- Corrected SDK error text (post-replay wording fix).

## 3. Selected behavior (specification)

### 3.1 Client (participating SDKs)

- Pre-transmission check: if batch size > 8,000 points, reject locally.
- Caller-facing instruction: "split the batch and retry with smaller batches."
- No HTTP request is issued for the oversized batch.
- No client-side retry of the oversized batch itself.

### 3.2 Server (ingest-edge)

- Receives a batch that exceeds the cap from an older or nonconforming client.
- Response: HTTP 413 (whole-batch rejection — no partial acceptance).
- Counters on the rejected request:
  - accepted = 0
  - rejected = submitted_count
  - reason = `oversized_batch`
- Behavior is deterministic and identical to the replay-validated contract.

### 3.3 Layering rationale (permanent)

- New clients get a fast, clear failure path with no network cost.
- Older / nonconforming clients continue to get a deterministic, well-countered 413 at the edge.
- Both paths emit the same `oversized_batch` reason and identical counter semantics, so observability and accounting converge.

## 4. Stop checks (must hold during enablement through 2025-01-28)

These checks must remain true as each stage turns on. If any check fails, halt the rollout and revert the in-progress stage.

1. Unchanged-retry check: client-side retry behavior on NON-oversized batches is unchanged. Oversized batches are not auto-retried by the client; smaller follow-up batches must succeed normally.
2. Accounting check:
   - For oversized batches: accepted = 0, rejected = submitted_count, reason = `oversized_batch` (every request, every region).
   - For in-limit batches: counters and accounting are unchanged from the pre-rollout baseline.
   - No new drift between client-reported and ingest-edge-reported batch sizes.

## 5. Rollout plan through 2025-01-28

- Enablement is staged, not a single big-bang cutover.
- Window: 2025-01-14 through 2025-01-28.
- Per stage (each participating SDK + ingest-edge slice):
  - Turn on the new pre-transmission check (client) and/or the retained 413 contract (server).
  - Verify the two stop checks above against the staged traffic.
  - Record results before proceeding to the next stage.
- Cutover is considered COMPLETE only when:
  - All participating SDKs have shipped the pre-transmission rejection.
  - ingest-edge is confirmed on the permanent 413 contract across all regions.
  - Both stop checks have held across the full window.

## 6. Open items

- Rollout is not complete as of 2025-01-14. Per-stage results (which SDKs are on, which ingest-edge regions are on, stop-check deltas) to be appended as enablement proceeds through 2025-01-28.
- Older-client behavior confirmed via the replay; no further contract change expected unless a stage surfaces one.
- Corrected SDK error text is the authoritative caller-facing wording for "split and retry smaller batches."

## 7. References

- Replay results (reviewed 2025-01-14).
- Current-client compatibility report (reviewed 2025-01-14).
- Older-client compatibility report (reviewed 2025-01-14).
- Corrected SDK error text (reviewed 2025-01-14).
- Existing oversized-batch v2 contract: 413 + counters (accepted=0, rejected=submitted) + `oversized_batch` + client-no-retry.

messages.content: [2025-01-17T09:20:00-05:00] Here is the `sphere-sdk-java#734` staged-enablement diff and test: The validator returns the programmatic `oversized_batch` error for more than 8,000 points. The catch block then places the original request object on `genericTransientRetryQueue`. The test expects zero immediate sends and one later send of that unchanged object.
I'll do a quick grounding check before responding — looking for any prior context on this PR and confirming the queue mechanics.

A critical inconsistency shows up. Before I respond to your "stage enablement" framing, I need to flag it.

**Stopping condition hit — this PR as described should not be staged.**

The supermemory record dated 2024-12-24 establishes the *current* SDK contract: the oversized-batch validation is a local, *programmatic* error telling the caller to split the batch. That is the baseline, and `sphere-sdk-java#734` as you described it **contradicts that contract in two ways**:

1. **It's routing an oversized batch onto `genericTransientRetryQueue`.** That queue is for transient transport/connection failures (cf. the collector-agent#152 transient-connection retry policy — exponential backoff with full jitter on transient errors). An oversized payload is not transient. Retrying it without changing it produces the same 413 every time, burns queue slots, and the SDK's "split the batch" instruction to the caller is bypassed. This is the *exact* shape of the bug the permanent oversized-batch design ([hr1zgcRs6b…](cQeG3qYHmFBmQppMxTMS7r)) was meant to prevent.

2. **The test expectation ("zero immediate sends, one later send of that unchanged object") encodes that wrong behavior.** If the validator rejects, the SDK's job is done — the caller decides whether to split, shrink, or drop. Queueing and replaying the *same* oversized object is precisely the client-retry behavior the v2 contract ([hr1zgcRs6boa12JKyJMRW2](cQeG3qYHmFBmQppMxTMS7r): 413 + accepted=0, rejected=submitted, `oversized_batch`, **client-no-retry**) was negotiated to forbid.

Memory entry [2024-11-27] in my notes is the parallel reference for the *server-side* v2 contract (413 + counters + `oversized_batch` + no-retry). The client side has to match.

**What I'd need before I'd support enabling this:**

- The exact `sphere-sdk-java#734` diff (I tried `get_pr`; arg shape needs `pr_id` as a string — happy to pull it if you want a line-by-line review).
- The matching server-side change in `ingest-edge` that makes `oversized_batch` non-retryable on the client — without it, a queued replay will get a 413 and the SDK will (correctly, per current policy) keep retrying, producing a tight loop against a 413-stamped error. Memory note [2025-01-06] has the Lantern alert-class / op-handoff closed on this, so the server contract should be stable enough to point at.
- Clarification of who owns the client-retry decision while `sphere-sdk-java#734` is staged. My note says "After the SDK generic retry is disabled and the two counters are added, the client owner is expected to provide a short confirmation" ([VjqcNH7Xc1SMygYNopgaGU](cQeG3qYHmFBmQppMxTMS7r)) — that's the handoff point. If `#734` re-enables a generic retry path for a *validation* failure (not a transport failure), it's reversing that handoff, not extending it.

**Bottom line:** I would not stage this. The diff as described puts a non-transient validation failure onto a transient retry queue and writes a test that locks that behavior in. Both should be reversed before enablement — either the validator stays a hard, caller-visible programmatic error (current contract), or the queueing path is *only* for transport-class failures and explicitly excludes validator rejections, with a separate test for that exclusion.

Want me to pull the PR body and the linked server-side commit, and draft the blocking review comment?

arguments.body:
# Oversized-batch handling (v2) — Decision and rollout through 2025-01-28

Date of decision: 2025-01-14
Owners: SDK (participating clients) + ingest-edge
Status: Decision LOCKED. Enablement staged through 2025-01-28. Rollout NOT complete.

## 1. Decision summary

After reviewing the completed replay, current- and older-client compatibility results, and the corrected SDK error text, the responsible owners selected the layered permanent oversized-batch design:

- Participating SDKs reject batches above 8,000 points BEFORE transmission and tell the caller to split them.
- ingest-edge retains deterministic HTTP 413 whole-batch rejection for older or nonconforming clients, with:
  - accepted points = 0
  - rejected points = submitted count
  - reason = `oversized_batch`
- The design is permanent (not a temporary cap), and is layered across client and server.

## 2. Inputs the owners reviewed

- Completed replay of the oversized-batch handling changes.
- Current-client compatibility results.
- Older-client compatibility results.
- Corrected SDK error text (post-replay wording fix).

## 3. Selected behavior (specification)

### 3.1 Client (participating SDKs)

- Pre-transmission check: if batch size > 8,000 points, reject locally.
- Caller-facing instruction: "split the batch and retry with smaller batches."
- No HTTP request is issued for the oversized batch.
- No client-side retry of the oversized batch itself.

### 3.2 Server (ingest-edge)

- Receives a batch that exceeds the cap from an older or nonconforming client.
- Response: HTTP 413 (whole-batch rejection — no partial acceptance).
- Counters on the rejected request:
  - accepted = 0
  - rejected = submitted_count
  - reason = `oversized_batch`
- Behavior is deterministic and identical to the replay-validated contract.

### 3.3 Layering rationale (permanent)

- New clients get a fast, clear failure path with no network cost.
- Older / nonconforming clients continue to get a deterministic, well-countered 413 at the edge.
- Both paths emit the same `oversized_batch` reason and identical counter semantics, so observability and accounting converge.

## 4. Stop checks (must hold during enablement through 2025-01-28)

These checks must remain true as each stage turns on. If any check fails, halt the rollout and revert the in-progress stage.

1. Unchanged-retry check: client-side retry behavior on NON-oversized batches is unchanged. Oversized batches are not auto-retried by the client; smaller follow-up batches must succeed normally.
2. Accounting check:
   - For oversized batches: accepted = 0, rejected = submitted_count, reason = `oversized_batch` (every request, every region).
   - For in-limit batches: counters and accounting are unchanged from the pre-rollout baseline.
   - No new drift between client-reported and ingest-edge-reported batch sizes.

- Cutover is considered COMPLETE only when:

sdk-go#1842 — inspection and review

PR
- id: sdk-go#1842
- title: "sdk-go: allow oversized metric batches with partial ingest"
- author / assignee: Mira
- reviewer: Alex
- status: open; opened 2027-12-29
- branch: mira/partial-oversized-batches
- stated intent (from PR description): "Remove the client-side maximum batch-size check so callers can transmit batches above the supported point limit. Ingest-edge is expected to process the supported prefix and reject only the remainder, allowing callers to inspect the partial result."

Tool returned no diff payload — `get_pr` only exposes the metadata above. The analysis below is against the stated intent plus the established contract.

Verdict: request_changes. The PR contradicts the LOCKED oversized-batch design on every dimension and would silently change ingest-edge's contract for one client.

1. Contradicts the LOCKED layered permanent design

The oversized-batch decision was LOCKED on 2025-01-14 and the rollout was completed through 2025-01-28 (recorded in the rollout doc and the post-completion comment on that doc). The selected design is:

- Client (participating SDKs): reject batches above 8,000 points pre-transmission, tell caller to "split the batch and retry with smaller batches," no HTTP request, no client-side retry of the oversized object.
- Server (ingest-edge): deterministic HTTP 413 whole-batch rejection for any oversized batch that reaches it (older/nonconforming clients), with accepted=0, rejected=submitted_count, reason=`oversized_batch`.

sdk-go#1842 proposes to:

- Remove the SDK-side 8,000 cap so callers can transmit above the limit.
- Have ingest-edge accept a "supported prefix" and reject only the remainder.
- Surface the partial result to the caller.

That is the partial-acceptance design that was explicitly deferred during the 2024-11-27 oversized-batch v2 contract negotiation and then explicitly rejected when the layered permanent design was chosen (discard / quarantine / hold / partial were the deferred permanent dispositions; partial was not selected).

2. Specific contract breaks

a. Client-side pre-transmission rejection removed
   - LOCKED: `pointCount >= 8000` → reject locally, zero network sends.
   - This PR: cap is removed; oversized objects are transmitted.
   - Consequence: re-enables the exact "non-transient validation failure on a transient retry queue" failure mode that was identified and rejected in the sphere-sdk-java#734 staged-enablement review. If sdk-go mirrors the queue behavior, an unchanged oversized object will hit ingest-edge, get 413, and replay into a tight loop.

b. Ingest-edge whole-batch rejection → partial acceptance
   - LOCKED (and reaffirmed by ingest-edge PR 2588 on 2027-05-11): 8,001 / 8,500 / any-oversize → HTTP 413, accepted=0, rejected=submitted, reason=`oversized_batch`. Deterministic, identical across encodings.
   - This PR: ingest-edge is expected to ingest the in-limit prefix and return the rejected remainder.
   - Consequence: the counter contract breaks. accepted_points for a single request is no longer 0 for an oversized batch; rejected_points is no longer the full submitted count. The accounting stop check ("no drift between client-reported and ingest-edge-reported batch sizes") fails by construction, and the rejection-reason label no longer identifies a clean whole-batch rejection.

c. Caller-facing semantics changed
   - LOCKED: caller gets a deterministic "split and retry" path.
   - This PR: caller gets a 200-style partial success with two sub-results, requiring the caller to inspect and resubmit the remainder. That is a new caller contract, not a continuation of the prior one.

d. Layering rationale inverted
   - LOCKED layering: new clients get a fast, zero-network-cost failure; older clients fall back to a deterministic 413 at the edge. Both paths emit the same reason and counter semantics.
   - This PR: only one SDK (sdk-go) diverges from the layered design. Other participating SDKs still pre-transmission-reject; older clients still 413. Observability and accounting now diverge across SDK lineage rather than converge.

3. Risks specific to partial-ingest semantics

a. Atomicity and replay. A "supported prefix + rejected remainder" response is not an atomic outcome. If ingest-edge ack succeeds and the caller fails to inspect / resubmit the remainder, those points are silently dropped — there is no 413, no `oversized_batch` counter, no alarm. The current contract trades a whole-batch failure for a partial-success path that is easier to silently lose data on.

b. Encoded-body edge case. ingest-edge PR 2588 fixed a compressed-body bypass where the original cap was checked on compressed Content-Length pre-decode. The corrected gate is "validate after bounded decode, before accept/enqueue." A partial-acceptance path has to define where it splits: by point count after decode? by decoded byte boundary? at the first malformed point? This needs explicit specification and replay evidence before any client could rely on it, and that work hasn't been done.

c. Older-client compatibility. Older clients (and other participating SDKs that still pre-transmit-reject) will continue to hit the 413 contract. Two client populations, two contracts, one ingest-edge. That is the exact shape that the layered design was built to avoid.

d. Callers that currently rely on `oversized_batch` as the sole signal of an oversize condition (dashboards, alerts, capacity planning) will see that signal disappear for sdk-go callers and replace it with a partial-success that the dashboard does not currently count.

4. What the PR would need to do to be acceptable

If the goal is genuinely to support partial-oversized ingest (which was deliberately deferred during the 2024-11-27 contract), then:

- Restart the design discussion with the SDK + ingest-edge owners. The LOCKED status must be reopened by the same owners who locked it, not unilaterally by one SDK contributor.
- Add a server-side proposal in ingest-edge that defines: split point, atomicity guarantees, new counter semantics (`partial_ingest_accepted` / `partial_ingest_rejected`), and a fresh replay covering both encodings and the compressed-body path that PR 2588 fixed.
- Update the oversized-batch rollout document to reflect the new design and the reason the LOCKED design is being superseded.
- Re-run current- and older-client compatibility evidence.
- Confirm both stop checks (unchanged-retry and accounting) still hold across the rollout window.

None of those have been proposed in this PR. As written, sdk-go#1842 is a unilateral contract change by one SDK author.

Recommended action

- Review decision: request_changes.
- Comment to Mira: PR removes the LOCKED client-side 8,000 cap and asks ingest-edge to do partial acceptance, which inverts the layered permanent design (413 whole-batch, accepted=0, rejected=submitted, reason=`oversized_batch`, client-no-retry) confirmed in the rollout doc and reaffirmed by ingest-edge PR 2588. Partial-acceptance semantics were explicitly deferred during the 2024-11-27 contract and not selected when the design was locked 2025-01-14. The change also breaks the accounting stop check by construction and creates silent-drop risk on the caller-inspects-remainder path. Ask for: either revert to the LOCKED client-side cap, or open a design proposal that reopens the LOCKED decision with both owners (SDK + ingest-edge) and a server-side spec + replay before this can ship.
- Hold the actual `review_pr` submission until you confirm; this is an irreversible write to the PR thread.

arguments.body:
# Q1 2027 platform workstreams — Lantern, Guardrails, and owner map

Owner of this document: Alex (reviewer role: shared-contract and failure-boundary).
Status as of 2027-01-11: living document. Sections below reflect the December 17
final decision, the December 28 kickoff-prep framing, the December 29 participant
proposals, and the January 11 staff-only rehearsal acceptance checklist.
Nothing here authorizes customer exposure or transfers routine implementation
ownership to Alex.

================================================================
1. APPROVED SPLIT (unchanged from December 17 review)
================================================================

Q1 2027 is three linked workstreams, not one Lantern monolith:

  - Lantern          — owns explanation and navigation. Reference-only.
  - Cardinality      — owns pipeline limits and cost semantics (authoritative).
    Guardrails
  - Owner map        — owns published responsibility (authoritative).

Lantern implementation is owned by Product Engineering. Alex is not the routine
implementation gate for any of the three workstreams. Alex reviews the shared
five-field contract and the cross-system failure boundaries only.

Lantern does not absorb owner-map data or Cardinality Guardrails data. Lantern
does not write into published responsibility. Lantern does not place limit or
cost data on a customer surface.

================================================================
2. FIVE-FIELD SHARED REFERENCE CONTRACT
================================================================

Per the December 17 review, internal Lantern cards may navigate staff to
authoritative owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails records using ONLY these
five fields — no others:

  1. tenant_id
  2. canonical_service_id
  3. authority_type
  4. authority_record_id
  5. source_timestamp

Rules of use:
  - Each reference carries exactly these five fields and nothing more.
  - Owner-map references and Cardinality Guardrails references carry
    SEPARATE authority identities and SEPARATE source timestamps — they
    are not collapsed into one reference and never share an
    authority_record_id.
  - If an authority record is stale (source_timestamp older than the
    freshness threshold for that authority_type) or missing (no current
    authority_record_id), Lantern MUST render the reference as explicit
    "unknown" with the stale/missing field shown — it does NOT guess,
    default, copy from cache, or fall back to a payload value.
  - Lantern MUST NOT copy any authority payload value into the card.
  - Lantern MUST NOT offer mutation capability into either authority.
  - On a denial (stale, missing, or out-of-scope), Lantern MUST NOT issue
    any adapter call afterwards. Zero adapter calls after denial.
  - These rules apply equally to staff-only and internal-shadow surfaces.

================================================================
3. JANUARY 22 STAFF-ONLY REHEARSAL — ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST
================================================================

Rehearsal date: 2027-01-22. Audience: staff only. Purpose: dry-run the
internal operating use of Lantern references against live authority records,
under the December 17 rules. The rehearsal is NOT a customer-exposure
authorization and is NOT a transfer of routine implementation ownership to
Alex. Product Engineering remains the implementation owner for the rehearsal
slice. Alex reviews whether the slice meets this checklist.

Pass criteria — every item MUST hold. A single failure blocks "passed."

  [A] Reference shape
      A.1  Every Lantern reference emitted during the rehearsal carries
           ONLY tenant_id, canonical_service_id, authority_type,
           authority_record_id, and source_timestamp.
      A.2  No reference carries any additional field, annotation, payload
           value, computed derivation, or display string derived from the
           authority payload.

  [B] Separate identities and source timestamps
      B.1  Every owner-map reference carries its own authority_record_id
           and its own source_timestamp.
      B.2  Every Cardinality Guardrails reference carries its own
           authority_record_id and its own source_timestamp.
      B.3  No reference shares an authority_record_id between owner-map
           and Cardinality Guardrails.
      B.4  No reference collapses the two authorities into a single
           combined reference.

  [C] Stale or missing authority records
      C.1  A reference whose source_timestamp is older than the freshness
           threshold for its authority_type is rendered as EXPLICIT
           "unknown — stale authority_record" with the
           authority_record_id and source_timestamp still shown (no
           hiding, no caching past the value).
      C.2  A reference with no current authority_record_id is rendered as
           EXPLICIT "unknown — no current authority_record" with
           tenant_id and canonical_service_id still shown.

# Q1 2027 platform workstreams — Lantern, Guardrails, and owner map

Status: Closeout — first-slice operating-evidence review (2027-02-18). Last updated 2027-02-18.

Reference for the January 7, 2027 Q1 platform-workstreams kickoff. Customer-path isolation is preserved across all sections below.

Note on reconstruction: the prior body of this document was overwritten during a probe that targeted an unknown doc_id; the content below is rebuilt from authoritative memory and the four accepted deliverables, and the new closeout (sections AE–AH) is the source of truth for the 2027-02-18 decision. Earlier section lettering is preserved where the underlying content is still known.

## Authority lanes (unchanged)

- Owner map owns published responsibility. It is the named authority for the responsibility lane; a blank-owner map case is fixed at the owner-map source.
- Cardinality Guardrails owns the controls and operating-limit semantics (e.g., the metrics-router pending-batch cap = 64/tenant). The dashboard review remains within the user's metrics-router operating-control lane because Cardinality Guardrails is the named authority for that scope.
- Lantern is a reference, explanation, and linking layer. It must not copy authority payload values, must not write back to the owner map or Guardrails records, and must not perform a writeback or CSV export. Option B keeps Cardinality Guardrails authoritative for the control, the 64-pending-batches-per-tenant limit, and cost semantics.
- Insertion order determines which authority survives when owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references collide in the shared Lantern contract; the first internal slice preserves separate `authority_type`, `authority_record_id`, and `source_timestamp` values for each, keyed on `(tenant_id, canonical_service_id, authority_type, authority_record_id)`.

## Customer-path exclusion (preserved)

- Customer authorization for Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce remains a separate later authorization and is out of scope for the January 7, 2027 kickoff.
- Lantern internal-reference checks for requests, artifacts, and outputs are recorded separately from customer counts and kept outside both customer paths.
- The first internal Lantern slice produces no output on Harbor or Mosaic customer paths; the owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references are read-only.
- Cross-tenant isolation covers requests, artifacts, and outputs across the Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce tenant boundary.

## Provisional scope

- Provisional authorization for the operating-evidence work runs through 2027-03-15. No post-3/15 authority is established by this review. The Lantern evidence cycle remains open through 2027-03-15.

## Sections A–L (kickoff and intent)

Original kickoff framing, interface, and first-deliverable list established at the January 7, 2027 Q1 platform-workstreams kickoff. The four first slices approved at kickoff are:

1. Lantern staff-only reference-card rendering that preserves separate owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references for the same canonical service.
2. Cardinality Guardrails controls navigability from Lantern internal cards.
3. Iris wording review on dual-reference cards (no authority transfer, no write-control presentation).
4. Customer-path zero-count for Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce (internal reference-only integration).

## Sections M–P (partial, 2027-02-18)

The 2027-02-18 review packet's sections M–P were still partial at the closeout review and are listed in the appendix for owner follow-through; they are not promoted to closure here.

## Sections Q–T (corrected-slice closeout, 2027-02-04)

On 2027-02-04 at 3:18 PM Eastern, the shared-contract block for the Q1 2027 Lantern workstream was closed after the corrected staff-only rerun. Closure belongs to the contract owner; the user does not close the Q–T shared-contract block on the contract owner's behalf. The corrected slice remains available for continuing internal use as a reference-only slice under the corrected five-field contract (`canonical_service_id`, `published_service_id`, `provenance_source`, `source_event_id`, `source_timestamp`); a record is rejected if any field is missing.

## Sections U–Y (owner-led observation, 2027-02-18)

Sections U–Y remain an owner-led observation rather than a user-owned closure; broader Q–T scope remained open despite the corrected-slice closure.

## Sections AA–AD (first-week checkpoint, 2027-02-11)

The February 11, 2027 checkpoint did not expand authorization, did not establish broader Q1 completion, did not close the full-window customer-path audit, and did not establish a final two-week tally. Section AD explicitly labeled the status unfinished.

## Sections AE–AH (first-slice closeout, 2027-02-18) — Hema's completion decision

Review attendees: Alex, the user, Hema, Iris, Cyrus, Wes, and Product Engineering. Window: 10:30–11:15 AM Eastern, 2027-02-18.

AE. Hema's completion decision.

Hema accepted all four first deliverables as complete at the first-slice operating-evidence closeout review. The decision is provisional through 2027-03-15 and does not establish any post-3/15 authority. Authority lanes remain unchanged. Customer-path exclusion is preserved.

AF. Complete final evidence (2027-02-04 through 2027-02-18).

1. Lantern staff-only ref-card rendering (deliverable 1).
   - 52 staff-only reference-card renders produced across the 2027-02-05 through 2027-02-18 window.
   - 19 of the 52 cards carried both owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references; the remainder carried exactly one authority reference.
   - All 24 dual-authority cases preserved separate owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references in both insertion orders, using the four-part identity `(tenant_id, canonical_service_id, authority_type, authority_record_id)` and each preserving its own `source_timestamp`.
   - On 2026-11-17, the dual-reference card navigated from the metrics-router service view to the Cardinality Guardrails record governing the 64-pending-batches-per-tenant control.

2. Cardinality Guardrails controls navigability (deliverable 2).
   - 11 of 11 controls navigable from the Lantern internal surface via the staff-only reference cards.
   - Wes reached the authoritative pre-acceptance backpressure record without copying its value into Lantern; backpressure is not held in Lantern.
   - Beginning 2026-12-17, Lantern internal cards may navigate staff to authoritative owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails records.

3. Iris wording review (deliverable 3).
   - Iris reviewed the corrected staff-only reference slice of Lantern PR #1226 on 2027-02-04 and found that none of the 24 dual-reference cards presented either linked record as a transfer of authority.
   - No reviewed card in the corrected Lantern PR #1226 staff-only reference slice presents a write control; display-name-only records are out of scope, and no alias or fallback identity may be used.
   - On 2026-11-18, Iris found no Lantern dual-reference wording that presented either the owner-map link or the Cardinality Guardrails link as a Lantern-owned value, a write control, or a transfer of authority.

4. Customer-path zero-count for Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce (deliverable 4).

# Q1 2027 platform workstreams — Lantern, Guardrails, and owner map

Status: Closeout — first-slice operating-evidence review (2027-02-18). Last updated 2027-02-18.

Reference for the January 7, 2027 Q1 platform-workstreams kickoff. Customer-path isolation is preserved across all sections below.

Note on reconstruction: the prior body of this document was overwritten during a probe that targeted an unknown doc_id; the content below is rebuilt from authoritative memory and the four accepted deliverables, and the new closeout (sections AE–AH) is the source of truth for the 2027-02-18 decision. Earlier section lettering is preserved where the underlying content is still known.

## Authority lanes (unchanged)

- Owner map owns published responsibility. It is the named authority for the responsibility lane; a blank-owner map case is fixed at the owner-map source.
- Cardinality Guardrails owns the controls and operating-limit semantics (e.g., the metrics-router pending-batch cap = 64/tenant). The dashboard review remains within the user's metrics-router operating-control lane because Cardinality Guardrails is the named authority for that scope.
- Lantern is a reference, explanation, and linking layer. It must not copy authority payload values, must not write back to the owner map or Guardrails records, and must not perform a writeback or CSV export. Option B keeps Cardinality Guardrails authoritative for the control, the 64-pending-batches-per-tenant limit, and cost semantics.
- Insertion order determines which authority survives when owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references collide in the shared Lantern contract; the first internal slice preserves separate `authority_type`, `authority_record_id`, and `source_timestamp` values for each, keyed on `(tenant_id, canonical_service_id, authority_type, authority_record_id)`.

## Customer-path exclusion (preserved)

- Customer authorization for Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce remains a separate later authorization and is out of scope for the January 7, 2027 kickoff.
- Lantern internal-reference checks for requests, artifacts, and outputs are recorded separately from customer counts and kept outside both customer paths.
- The first internal Lantern slice produces no output on Harbor or Mosaic customer paths; the owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references are read-only.
- Cross-tenant isolation covers requests, artifacts, and outputs across the Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce tenant boundary.

## Provisional scope

- Provisional authorization for the operating-evidence work runs through 2027-03-15. No post-3/15 authority is established by this review. The Lantern evidence cycle remains open through 2027-03-15.

## Sections A–L (kickoff and intent)

Original kickoff framing, interface, and first-deliverable list established at the January 7, 2027 Q1 platform-workstreams kickoff. The four first slices approved at kickoff are:

1. Lantern staff-only reference-card rendering that preserves separate owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references for the same canonical service.
2. Cardinality Guardrails controls navigability from Lantern internal cards.
3. Iris wording review on dual-reference cards (no authority transfer, no write-control presentation).
4. Customer-path zero-count for Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce (internal reference-only integration).

## Sections M–P (partial, 2027-02-18)

The 2027-02-18 review packet's sections M–P were still partial at the closeout review and are listed in the appendix for owner follow-through; they are not promoted to closure here.

## Sections Q–T (corrected-slice closeout, 2027-02-04)

On 2027-02-04 at 3:18 PM Eastern, the shared-contract block for the Q1 2027 Lantern workstream was closed after the corrected staff-only rerun. Closure belongs to the contract owner; the user does not close the Q–T shared-contract block on the contract owner's behalf. The corrected slice remains available for continuing internal use as a reference-only slice under the corrected five-field contract (`canonical_service_id`, `published_service_id`, `provenance_source`, `source_event_id`, `source_timestamp`); a record is rejected if any field is missing.

## Sections U–Y (owner-led observation, 2027-02-18)

Sections U–Y remain an owner-led observation rather than a user-owned closure; broader Q–T scope remained open despite the corrected-slice closure.

## Sections AA–AD (first-week checkpoint, 2027-02-11)

The February 11, 2027 checkpoint did not expand authorization, did not establish broader Q1 completion, did not close the full-window customer-path audit, and did not establish a final two-week tally. Section AD explicitly labeled the status unfinished.

## Sections AE–AH (first-slice closeout, 2027-02-18) — Hema's completion decision

Review attendees: Alex, the user, Hema, Iris, Cyrus, Wes, and Product Engineering. Window: 10:30–11:15 AM Eastern, 2027-02-18.

AE. Hema's completion decision.

Hema accepted all four first deliverables as complete at the first-slice operating-evidence closeout review. The decision is provisional through 2027-03-15 and does not establish any post-3/15 authority. Authority lanes remain unchanged. Customer-path exclusion is preserved.

AF. Complete final evidence (2027-02-04 through 2027-02-18).

1. Lantern staff-only ref-card rendering (deliverable 1).
   - 52 staff-only reference-card renders produced across the 2027-02-05 through 2027-02-18 window.
   - 19 of the 52 cards carried both owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references; the remainder carried exactly one authority reference.
   - All 24 dual-authority cases preserved separate owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references in both insertion orders, using the four-part identity `(tenant_id, canonical_service_id, authority_type, authority_record_id)` and each preserving its own `source_timestamp`.
   - On 2026-11-17, the dual-reference card navigated from the metrics-router service view to the Cardinality Guardrails record governing the 64-pending-batches-per-tenant control.

2. Cardinality Guardrails controls navigability (deliverable 2).
   - 11 of 11 controls navigable from the Lantern internal surface via the staff-only reference cards.
   - Wes reached the authoritative pre-acceptance backpressure record without copying its value into Lantern; backpressure is not held in Lantern.
   - Beginning 2026-12-17, Lantern internal cards may navigate staff to authoritative owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails records.

3. Iris wording review (deliverable 3).
   - Iris reviewed the corrected staff-only reference slice of Lantern PR #1226 on 2027-02-04 and found that none of the 24 dual-reference cards presented either linked record as a transfer of authority.
   - No reviewed card in the corrected Lantern PR #1226 staff-only reference slice presents a write control; display-name-only records are out of scope, and no alias or fallback identity may be used.
   - On 2026-11-18, Iris found no Lantern dual-reference wording that presented either the owner-map link or the Cardinality Guardrails link as a Lantern-owned value, a write control, or a transfer of authority.

4. Customer-path zero-count for Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce (deliverable 4).
   - Through 2027-01-26 and continuing through 2027-02-18, the Lantern internal reference-only integration produced 0 requests, 0 artifacts, and 0 outputs on the Harbor Health customer path.
   - Through 2027-01-26 and continuing through 2027-02-18, the Lantern internal reference-only integration produced 0 requests, 0 artifacts, and 0 outputs on the Mosaic Commerce customer path.
   - The Q1 Lantern reference slice produced no output for Mosaic Commerce; the first internal slice produces no output on either customer path.

AG. Open items (not closed by the 2027-02-18 review).

- Sections M–P remain partial.
- Broader Q–T scope remains open despite the corrected-slice closure.
- Sections U–Y are owner-led observation, not user-owned closure.
- The full Q1 2027 customer-preview evidence period (2027-01-01 through 2027-03-15) remains open; final counts are frozen and reconciled on 2027-03-15, not earlier.
- Freshness thresholds per `authority_type` and the legal enum values for `authority_type` remain open questions.
- The deny-path exercise for the zero-adapter-call check is left as an open question.

AH. Next update trigger.

The next update trigger is the observation-window close (2027-03-15), an out-of-band split change, or Hema's next completion decision.

## Appendix — sources and timestamps

- 2026-09-19: Q1 2027 platform workstreams split proposed (owner map = published responsibility; Cardinality Guardrails = controls; Lantern = reference layer).
- 2026-11-12: 120 Lantern fixture runs; 24 dual-authority cases preserved separate references in both insertion orders.
- 2026-11-17: Dual-reference card navigated from metrics-router service view to Cardinality Guardrails record governing the 64-pending-batches-per-tenant control.
- 2026-11-18: Iris wording review — no dual-reference card presented a transfer of authority.
- 2026-12-17: Lantern internal cards may navigate staff to authoritative owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails records.
- 2027-01-01: Lantern customer-preview evidence period began for Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce.
- 2027-01-07: Q1 platform-workstreams kickoff completed; all four first deliverables approved.
- 2027-01-26: First provisional Q1 checkpoint issued by Product Engineering covering 2027-01-01 through 2027-01-26.
- 2027-01-27: Provisional checkpoint through 2027-01-31 (141 logical explanation requests; 15 explicit-unknown outcomes; 94 eligible combined explanations under the 24-hour source-timestamp rule).
- 2027-02-04: Corrected staff-only rerun; corrected slice closed on the Q–T shared-contract block by the contract owner.
- 2027-02-04: Every reviewed card in the corrected staff-only Lantern PR #1226 reference slice named either the owner map or Cardinality Guardrails as the authority.
- 2027-02-05 through 2027-02-07: 6 of 18 staff-only reference-card renders carried both owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references.
- 2027-02-06: Hema confirmed the first-slice operating-evidence closeout review for Thursday, 2027-02-18.
- 2027-02-11: Sections AA–AD appended (first-week checkpoint; status unfinished).
- 2027-02-13: Next Lantern checkpoint targeted for the week of 2027-02-13 or an earlier out-of-band update from Product Engineering.
- 2027-02-18: First-slice operating-evidence closeout review (10:30–11:15 AM Eastern). Hema accepted all four first deliverables as complete. 52 staff-only reference-card renders produced; 19 carried both owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references; 11 of 11 controls navigable; Wes reached authoritative pre-acceptance backpressure record without copying into Lantern; Iris wording review held; Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce 0/0/0 IR (requests, artifacts, outputs). Authority lanes unchanged; customer-path exclusion preserved; provisional through 2027-03-15.

# Lantern internal reference slice — Feb 5–18, 2027 (evidence note)

## Window and scope

- Window: 2027-02-05 through 2027-02-18 (14 calendar days).
- Slice: Lantern "corrected first reference slice" — staff-only, internal reference-only, consuming only `tenant_id`, `canonical_service_id`, `authority_type`, `authority_record_id`, and `source_timestamp`. No copied authority payload values. No mutation, writeback, or CSV export. Five-field contract; a record is rejected if any field is missing.
- Set: at the 2027-02-06 one-on-one, Hema kept the broader 2027-01-01–2027-03-15 Lantern evidence cycle OPEN and agreed the corrected first reference slice should accumulate internal operating evidence through 2027-02-18.
- Closed: 2027-02-18 closeout review (10:30–11:15 ET). Attendees: Alex, the user, Hema, Iris, Cyrus, Wes, Product Engineering. Hema accepted all four first deliverables as complete on this slice.

## Use (what the slice was for)

1. Accumulate internal operating evidence on the corrected staff-only reference slice under the corrected five-field contract.
2. Demonstrate that staff-only reference cards render with dual owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references preserved, in both insertion orders, keyed on `(tenant_id, canonical_service_id, authority_type, authority_record_id)` with each reference's own `source_timestamp`.
3. Demonstrate Cardinality Guardrails controls are navigable from the Lantern internal surface without copying values back into Lantern (backpressure not held in Lantern).
4. Verify Iris wording-review closure carries forward on the live slice (no Lantern-owns-value/control, no write-control presentation, no alias or fallback identity; display-name-only records out of scope).
5. Maintain the per-tenant customer-path zero-count for Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce throughout the window (internal reference-only integration must produce 0 requests, 0 artifacts, 0 outputs on either customer path).

## Evidence recorded across the window

- Reference-card rendering: 52 staff-only renders in 2027-02-05–2027-02-18; 19 carried both owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references; 24 dual-authority cases preserved separate refs in both insertion orders. Sub-period 2027-02-05–2027-02-07 alone: 6 of 18 carried both.
- Controls navigability: 11 of 11 controls navigable from the Lantern internal surface via staff-only cards; Wes reached the authoritative pre-acceptance backpressure record without copying the value into Lantern.
- Iris wording: held closed on the live slice; none of the 24 dual-reference cards presented either linked record as a transfer of authority or as a write control.
- Customer-path zero-count: Harbor Health 0/0/0 and Mosaic Commerce 0/0/0 (requests / artifacts / outputs) from the Lantern internal reference-only integration across the window.

## Customer-path boundary (preserved)

- The slice is staff-only and internal-reference-only. It does not authorize, and is not connected to, any Harbor Health or Mosaic Commerce customer path.
- Internal-reference requests, artifacts, and outputs are recorded separately from customer counts and kept outside both customer paths.
- Cross-tenant isolation covers requests, artifacts, and outputs across the Harbor Health and Mosaic Commerce tenant boundary.
- No CSV export, no cost data, no writeback, no release-readiness judgment, no customer exposure of internal reference navigation is authorized on or because of this slice.
- Provisional authorization for the operating-evidence work runs through 2027-03-15; the 2027-02-18 acceptance does not establish any post-3/15 authority.

## Provisional status and what was NOT closed by this slice

- The 2027-01-01–2027-03-15 customer-preview evidence period stays open; final counts are frozen and reconciled on 2027-03-15, not 2027-02-18.
- Sections M–P of the workstream doc remain partial; broader Q–T scope remains open despite the corrected-slice closure; sections U–Y are owner-led observation, not user-owned closure.
- Open questions: freshness thresholds per `authority_type`; legal enum values for `authority_type`; deny-path exercise for the zero-adapter-call check.
- Authority lanes unchanged: owner map = published responsibility; Cardinality Guardrails = controls and operating-limit semantics; Lantern = reference and linking layer only.

## Sources

- 2027-02-06 1:1 with Hema — slice window set, broader Q1 not accepted, no ownership change, no production window, no customer auth change.
- 2027-02-18 first-slice operating-evidence closeout review — four deliverables accepted, evidence above recorded, lanes and customer-path exclusion preserved.
- Workstream doc: "Q1 2027 platform workstreams — Lantern, Guardrails, and owner map" (doc_dd2014a06d7b4d33958ed6986c1a5927).
- Slack closeout posted to #lantern (message id send_slack_message_da426c7aef7241bcb5938b1f3e99b699, 2027-02-18).

Alex 2026 self-review — evidence draft
Working draft for later revision. Bounded to IC role; no claim of managing people, owning every release, or becoming a centralized approval gate. Organized as Hema requested: cross-service invariants and failure modes, technical outcomes, owner leverage, and boundaries that kept routine implementation with mapped owners.

Frame: I review only where work crosses service boundaries or introduces new failure modes; otherwise it stays with mapped owners. Below are the concrete 2026 items that fit that frame, with the source artifacts that ground each claim.

1. Cross-service invariants and failure modes I reviewed

1.1 Authority boundaries and the Cardinality Guardrails design
- What: Defined the invariants that an authority record must preserve when an internal implementation slice attaches read-only owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references to the same canonical service. The invariants — authority_type + authority_record_id + source_timestamp — must be preserved unchanged; if no reference can be produced, the request is sent to Harbor/Mosaic rather than silently losing provenance.
- Why it crosses a boundary: owner-map references and Cardinality Guardrails touch the model used by Harbor, Mosaic, and downstream consumers. Changing how authority is referenced affects every service that reasons about identity. I treated this as a cross-service invariant, not a routine implementation decision, and surfaced the rule rather than letting it get absorbed into a single team's PR.
- Source: closed Lantern review doc_d52325f8b6044de0b34a61406dee62a5 (Oct 22 owner-boundary review, closed).
- Bounded to IC: I defined the invariant; the implementation slice is owned and merged by the mapped owner. I did not become the approval gate for the slice.

1.2 Duplicate-deploy dedup key
- What: Stated the dedup key as (tenant_id, published_service_id, provenance_source, source_event_id); missing any field → "unavailable" rather than best-guess.
- Why it crosses a boundary: dedup spans ingest-edge → metrics-router → shard-keeper. A wrong key in any one of them double-counts downstream; a too-loose key silently drops events. Pinning the key and the missing-field behavior was the cross-service invariant. The implementation in each service stayed with the mapped owner.
- Source: memory, 2025-08-12.

1.3 Tenant isolation for edge-gateway / ingest-edge
- What: Treated tenant isolation as a cross-service invariant, not a per-service detail, and insisted any change that could weaken tenant boundaries be reviewed across services.
- Why it crosses a boundary: a per-tenant bleed in edge-gateway or ingest-edge shows up as misattributed traffic or cardinality in metrics-router. Reviewing it at the boundary is where I add value.
- Source: closed Lantern review doc_d52325f8b6044de0b34a61406dee62a5 (scope of Alex review enumerated as: tenant isolation, provenance, auth source timestamps, authority duplication/mutation, customer-path isolation).

1.4 Provenance and auth source timestamps
- What: Reviewed changes touching how provenance_source and auth source timestamps flow through the pipeline, because a drift here corrupts the dedup key and the authority record in 1.1/1.2 simultaneously.
- Source: same closed doc as 1.1/1.3.

2. Technical outcomes

2.1 Mosaic forward-gate criteria, closed 2026-01-22
- What: Documented and validated the forward-gate criteria for Mosaic past the 17.2M forecast: 90 minutes at +15% load, q-p99 ≤ 400ms held for 5 minutes, queue-full ≤ 0.5% held for 5 minutes. Pre-accept backpressure is retryable. Capacity: 2,048 global / 64 per-tenant.
- Outcome: gate criteria were adopted as the cutover bar; the gate is documented (doc_1d054bf3238f4d44a691bb7e56c09937).
- Source: memory, 2026-01-22 entry.

2.2 shard-keeper#190 (Cyrus) cutover, closed 2026-09-17
- What: Confirmed the cutover was closed and scoped to replay-fixture cleanup. Pinned the gate: an id-carrying reject from a prior-epoch must be honored before any comms promise — i.e., verify the address before promising reachability. This is a concrete instance of "review only at boundaries that introduce new failure modes": the prior-epoch reject is exactly the kind of failure mode a comms-only check would have missed.
- Source: memory, 2026-09-17 entry.

2.3 Apr 14 shard-keeper / rollup-service outage
- What: Co-authored the postmortem (doc_postmortem_apr14_outage, 2026-04-21). The postmortem identifies the cross-service failure mode between shard-keeper and rollup-service.
- Bounded to IC: postmortem authorship is review-by-default, not ownership of either service's roadmap. Wes runs responder paths; Nadia runs postmortem process; I am one of the reviewers on cross-service failure cases.
- Source: doc_postmortem_apr14_outage.

3. Owner leverage: where I made a difference without becoming the owner

3.1 Metrics-router ownership transition (Wes primary, Alex backup)
- What: Stood up as backup on metrics-router during Hema's metrics migration so the cutover could proceed without single-point risk. Hema may reorder cutover; backup coverage is what kept the migration reversible.
- Outcome: Wes is the primary owner; I am backup only. The backup role was deliberately scoped to "present and able to act", not "second owner with parallel roadmap authority."
- Bounded to IC: I do not own metrics-router's roadmap, release cadence, or PR queue; I review at boundaries. This is leverage from being the right reviewer at the right moment, not leverage from accumulating ownership.
- Source: user profile; Hema collaboration note.

3.2 Lantern's corrected review routing
- What: The Lantern owner-model was validated as NOT an implementation / release-gate by Hema in the Oct 9 1:1. The routine Lantern work — copy, fixture-naming — stays with the mapped owner. I review only the cross-service slice: tenant isolation, provenance, auth source timestamps, authority duplication/mutation, customer-path isolation. This corrects an earlier drift where Lantern review could have been read as "Alex reviews Lantern changes" in general.
- Outcome: routing is now explicit and bounded. Routine → mapped owner; cross-service → Alex.
- Source: closed Lantern review doc_d52325f8b6044de0b34a61406dee62a5.

3.3 October 22 owner-boundary review (closed)
- What: At the Q4 owner-boundary review on 2026-10-22, two routine items were tested against my review scope: PE-routine Lantern copy / fixture-naming, and Wes-routine metrics-router staging route-cache param. Both were off-boundary for me and stayed with the mapped reviewers. The incident-practice split was preserved (Wes = responder paths, Nadia = postmortem process, Alex = cross-service failure cases only).
- Outcome: no ownership change, no centralized-gate creation, no Lantern first-slice decision, no internal-shadow decision, no customer/platform-scope decision triggered. The review closed with the boundary intact.
- Source: memory, 2026-10-22 entry.

4. Boundaries that kept routine implementation with mapped owners

4.1 I do not own releases. I review PRs that touch cross-service invariants (authority boundaries, dedup key, tenant isolation, provenance, customer-path isolation, prior-epoch gate semantics). I do not own metrics-router's release calendar, ingest-edge's deploys, or shard-keeper's cutover execution.

8.1 October 22, 2026 — owner-boundary review (routine stays with mapped owners)
- What I did: At the Q4 owner-boundary review I tested two routine items against my review scope: PE-routine Lantern copy / fixture-naming, and Wes-routine metrics-router staging route-cache param. Both were off-boundary for me and stayed with the mapped reviewers.
- Why this fits the framing: routine implementation work does not pull into my review queue even when the PR shows up next to ones that do. The boundary held without me declining in the abstract — the review itself was the disambiguator.
- Outcome: no ownership change, no centralized-gate creation, no Lantern first-slice decision, no internal-shadow decision, no customer/platform-scope decision triggered. Wes = responder paths, Nadia = postmortem process, Alex = cross-service failure cases only. Review closed with the boundary intact.

- Bounded to IC: I was a reviewer at the boundary meeting, not the meeting's owner; nothing here gives me a release authority, an approval queue, or a reviewer-of-record role on routine Lantern or metrics-router PRs.

- Trigger: corrected review routing surfaced an actual named boundary — an order-dependent overwrite between owner-map and Cardinality Guardrails references attached to the same canonical service. I did not take over Product Engineering's implementation of the fix.

2. Technical outcomes

2.1 Mosaic forward-gate criteria, closed 2026-01-22
- What: Documented and validated the forward-gate criteria for Mosaic past the 17.2M forecast: 90 minutes at +15% load, q-p99 ≤ 400ms held for 5 minutes, queue-full ≤ 0.5% held for 5 minutes. Pre-accept backpressure is retryable. Capacity: 2,048 global / 64 per-tenant.

2.3 Apr 14 shard-keeper / rollup-service outage
- What: Co-authored the postmortem (doc_postmortem_apr14_outage, 2026-04-21). The postmortem identifies the cross-service failure mode between shard-keeper and rollup-service.
- Bounded to IC: postmortem authorship is review-by-default, not ownership of either service's roadmap. Wes runs responder paths; Nadia runs postmortem process; I am one of the reviewers on cross-service failure cases.
- Source: doc_postmortem_apr14_outage.

3. Owner leverage: where I made a difference without becoming the owner

3.1 Metrics-router ownership transition (Wes primary, Alex backup)
- What: Stood up as backup on metrics-router during Hema's metrics migration so the cutover could proceed without single-point risk. Hema may reorder cutover; backup coverage is what kept the migration reversible.
- Outcome: Wes is the primary owner; I am backup only. The backup role was deliberately scoped to "present and able to act", not "second owner with parallel roadmap authority."
- Bounded to IC: I do not own metrics-router's roadmap, release cadence, or PR queue; I review at boundaries. This is leverage from being the right reviewer at the right moment, not leverage from accumulating ownership.
- Source: user profile; Hema collaboration note.

3.2 Lantern's corrected review routing
- What: The Lantern owner-model was validated as NOT an implementation / release-gate by Hema in the Oct 9 1:1. The routine Lantern work — copy, fixture-naming — stays with the mapped owner. I review only the cross-service slice: tenant isolation, provenance, auth source timestamps, authority duplication/mutation, customer-path isolation. This corrects an earlier drift where Lantern review could have been read as "Alex reviews Lantern changes" in general.
- Outcome: routing is now explicit and bounded. Routine → mapped owner; cross-service → Alex.
- Source: closed Lantern review doc_d52325f8b6044de0b34a61406dee62a5.

3.3 October 22 owner-boundary review (closed)
- What: At the Q4 owner-boundary review on 2026-10-22, two routine items were tested against my review scope: PE-routine Lantern copy / fixture-naming, and Wes-routine metrics-router staging route-cache param. Both were off-boundary for me and stayed with the mapped reviewers. The incident-practice split was preserved (Wes = responder paths, Nadia = postmortem process, Alex = cross-service failure cases only).
- Outcome: no ownership change, no centralized-gate creation, no Lantern first-slice decision, no internal-shadow decision, no customer/platform-scope decision triggered. The review closed with the boundary intact.
- Source: memory, 2026-10-22 entry.

4. Boundaries that kept routine implementation with mapped owners

4.1 I do not own releases. I review PRs that touch cross-service invariants (authority boundaries, dedup key, tenant isolation, provenance, customer-path isolation, prior-epoch gate semantics). I do not own metrics-router's release calendar, ingest-edge's deploys, or shard-keeper's cutover execution.

4.2 I do not manage people. I author and co-author postmortems and review docs; the people-management actions (hiring, leveling, performance, comp) are not part of my role and are not claimed here.

4.3 I do not act as a centralized approval gate. The Oct 22 review specifically confirmed: no ownership change, no centralized-gate creation. Routine work routes to mapped owners; my review appears only at the boundary.

4.4 Internal implementation slices may attach read-only owner-map + Cardinality Guardrails references to the same canonical service, and must preserve authority_type + authority_record_id + source_timestamp; no reference output routes to Harbor/Mosaic. I stated the invariant; the slice is implemented and merged by the mapped owner.

4.5 Incident practice split is intact and was reaffirmed on 2026-10-22: Wes owns responder paths, Nadia owns postmortem process, I review cross-service failure cases only.

5. Items I deliberately did not claim
- Did not claim to own metrics-router, ingest-edge, or shard-keeper.
- Did not claim to run the metrics migration (Hema runs it; I am a reviewer and backup).
- Did not claim to be the postmortem owner (Nadia owns the postmortem process; I am a reviewer and co-author on the cross-service cases).
- Did not claim to have approved or rejected any release on my own authority — my review appears at the boundary, the mapped owner decides.
- Did not claim any centralized approval role; the Oct 22 review explicitly foreclosed that interpretation.

6. Open items for revision before submission
- Confirm final dates and doc IDs above against current documents (doc_d52325f8b6044de0b34a61406dee62a5, doc_1d054bf3238f4d44a691bb7e56c09937, doc_postmortem_apr14_outage) — refresh references if any have moved.
